This gives compact support and smoothness without having to describe the boundary of the support.

papers.title: Solutions of the Riemann problem for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model
papers.abstract: The present paper is devoted to exhibit solutions of the Riemann problem for the Self-Organized Hydrodynamics model. The 2 x 2 system under consideration is strictly hyperbolic. With ambiguous non-conservative products, we adopt a non usual Generalized Rankine-Hugoniot jump condition to suitably define the shock wave solutions. This jump condition is obtained from the information given by the travelling wave solutions of the viscous extension of the system that involves the diffusion terms arising from the physics of the problem. We are then able to determine the simple waves of the non-conservative system studied here and we are able to construct some solutions of the Riemann problem of interest.

papers.title: Sharp helical maximal estimates in all dimensions
papers.abstract: We establish sharp $L^p$ maximal estimates for averages over smooth nondegenerate curves in $\mathbb R^n$ for $p>n$. More precisely, we show that for any nondegenerate curve $γ$ in $\mathbb R^n$ and the associated maximal operator \begin{equation} M f(x):=\sup_{t>0} \Big|\int_{-1}^1f(x-tγ(s))χ(s)\,\mathrm{d}s\Big|, \end{equation} the estimate \begin{equation} \| Mf\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)}\lesssim_{γ,p,n} \|f\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^n)} \end{equation} holds for all $p>n$. A new ingredient is a weighted Kakeya-type estimate.

papers.title: Quantum circuits of elastic wave equations via Schrödingerisation
papers.abstract: We construct explicit quantum circuits for the velocity-stress formulation of elastic wave equations in homogeneous media using Schrödingerisation. After rewriting the equations in symmetric matrix form(SMF), we use Fourier spectral discretization for source-driven periodic problems and staggered-grid finite differences for Dirichlet, Neumann, and impedance boundary conditions. The Schrödingerisation method transforms any linear PDEs into a system of Schrödinger-type PDEs -with unitary evolution- using the warped phase transformation that maps the equations in one higher dimension. For periodic problems, we develop circuits by combining controlled Fourier-mode rotations. For physical boundaries, interleaved encoding swaps the spatial and field-component registers, enabling a more efficient circuit construction using shift operators. We analyze $p$th-order Trotter-Suzuki formulas and derive splitting-error and CNOT-gate estimates, under the assumptions of smooth auxiliary initialization and solution-state recovery. Comparison with classical partitioned splitting methods identifies a polynomial improvement in spatial-resolution dependence for the quantum state-evolution subroutine. Noiseless circuit simulations of a forced periodic problem and an impedance problem illustrate the constructions and quantify their errors against exact solutions and classical reference computations.

papers.title: Non-convergence in heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics: The bounded influence model
papers.abstract: In a recent preprint, we found counterexamples to a number of auxiliary conjectures in a 2012 paper of Mirtabatabaei and Bullo, concerning convergence in two fundamental models of heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause dynamics, the synchronized bounded confidence (SBC) and synchronized bounded influence (SBI) models. Building on our work, Etesami and Touri presented an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBC dynamics, resolving the main conjecture from the 2012 paper in that case. Here we complete this project by presenting an example of an opinion vector which doesn't converge under SBI dynamics. The example was found with the help of AI.

papers.title: On the convexity of the fundamental domain of binary cyclotomic forms
papers.abstract: Denote by $Φ_m(X,Y)\in\Z[X,Y]$, $m\geqslant 1$ the sequence of binary cyclotomic forms, so that $Φ_m(T,1)\in\Z[T]$, $m\geqslant 1$ is the sequence of cyclotomic polynomials. We prove that, for $m\geqslant 3$, the fundamental domain $ \cal{O}_m:= \{ (x,y)\in\R^2\; \mid \; Φ_m(x,y)\leqslant 1\} $ of $Φ_m$ is a convex subset of $\R^2$ if and only if $m$ is equal to $p$, $2p$ or $2^k$ with $p$ an odd prime and $k\geqslant 2$. Finally we investigate the convexity of the fundamental domains attached to some products of binary forms $Φ_m$.

papers.title: On Landsberg Unicorns of General $(α,β)$-Type
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate the classes of \lq\lq unicorns" of general $(α,β)$-metric types, namely, Landsberg general $(α,β)$-metrics that are non-Berwaldian. We provide explicit solutions for these metrics, including several new classes. Furthermore, we identify and exclude the cases that yield degenerate metrics to guarantee the geometric validity of the established solutions.

papers.title: Three quantitative central limit theorems for the unbounded excursion component of a Gaussian field
papers.abstract: For a class of smooth stationary Gaussian fields, we study the fluctuations of the volume, surface area and Euler characteristic of the unbounded excursion component in growing boxes $Λ_n=[-n,n]^d$. We establish nondegenerate central limit theorems for all three functionals throughout the supercritical regime in every dimension $d\geq 2$. We further quantify these central limit theorems by establishing Berry--Esseen bounds of order $O\bigl(|Λ_n|^{-(1-1/s)}\bigr)$ in Kolmogorov distance, where $s\in(1,2]$ depend on the regularity and decay assumptions. Especially for the Bargmann--Fock field, we obtain a Berry--Esseen bound of $O\bigl(|Λ_n|^{-1/2}\bigr)$ for all three functionals. A matching lower bound shows that this rate is sharp for the Euler characteristic. For the volume, we improve the previously known rate of $O\bigl(|Λ_n|^{-1/2}(\log|Λ_n|)^{2d}\bigr)$. We mainly use Stein's method and moment bounds for differences arising from white-noise resampling to finish our proof.

papers.title: Global Existence and Scattering of a Class of Two-Dimensional Euler--Poisson--Korteweg Systems
papers.abstract: For a class of two-dimensional Euler--Poisson--Korteweg systems of quantum hydrodynamic type, we establish global existence and scattering for small, smooth, spatially localized perturbations of a constant equilibrium with irrotational velocity. This extends the three-dimensional well-posedness result of Song [Math. Ann. 392 (2025), 2157--2224] to two dimensions. Our proof follows the space-time resonance approach developed by Deng, Ionescu, Pausader, and Pusateri for the three-dimensional gravity-capillary water-wave system. The new ingredients are twofold. First, to allow non-neutral initial data, we exploit the absence of space resonances and of time resonances---including those arising after the second and third iterations---and the improved approximate-finite-speed-of-propagation bounds. Second, in the energy estimates, we adapt the almost orthogonality argument used in the works of Ionescu--Pausader and Guo--Ionescu--Pausader to the regime in which the input and output frequencies are all comparable to $1$. In this regime, time resonances may occur and the relevant curvature quantity may vanish.

papers.title: The homogeneity function of the fractional $p$-Laplacian and optimal asymptotic exponents for critical Hardy-Sobolev equations
papers.abstract: Let $N \geq 2$, $s\in (0,1)$, and $p \in (1, \infty)$ with $N>sp$. For the fractional $p$-Laplacian, the power function $|x|^{-γ}$ with $0<γ<\frac{N}{p-1}$ satisfies $$(-Δ_p)^s \big(|x|^{-γ}\big)=Φ(γ)|x|^{-γ(p-1)-sp} \, \text{ in }\mathbb{R}^N\setminus\{0\}.$$ Starting from the power function formula of Del Pezzo and Quaas (2026), we derive a paired integral representation of $Φ$, and show that $Φ$ is strictly increasing and then strictly decreasing, with a unique maximum at $\frac{N-sp}{p}$. This maximum $\barμ:=Φ(\frac{N-sp}{p})$ equals one half of the sharp fractional Hardy constant. Consequently, for every $0<μ<\barμ$, the equation $Φ(γ)=μ$ has exactly two roots $0<γ_{-}(μ)<\frac{N-sp}{p}<γ_{+}(μ)<\frac{N-sp}{p-1}$. These roots determine the homogeneous solutions $|x|^{-γ_{-}(μ)}$ and $|x|^{-γ_{+}(μ)}$ of the Hardy equation \begin{equation*} (-Δ_p)^s u - μ\frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{sp}}=0 \quad \text{in }\mathbb R^N\setminus\{0\}, \; u> 0 \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N \setminus \{0\}. \end{equation*} For $0<μ<\barμ$, we then study the following critical Hardy-Sobolev equation \begin{align}\tag{$\mathcal{P}$}\label{P} (-Δ_p)^s u-μ\frac{u^{p-1}}{|x|^{sp}} = u^{\frac{Np}{N-sp}-1} \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N, \; u > 0 \text{ in } \mathbb{R}^N. \end{align} Let $p \geq 2$ and $U$ be a positive, radially symmetric, nonincreasing finite-energy weak solution to \eqref{P}. We prove that there exists $C>0$ for which \begin{align*} U(x) \leq C|x|^{-γ_-(μ)}\;\text{as }|x| \rightarrow 0,\quad \text{ and } \quad U(x)\le C|x|^{-γ_+(μ)} \; \text{as }|x| \rightarrow \infty. \end{align*} Further, we show that $γ_-(μ)$ and $γ_+(μ)$ are the optimal exponents describing the singularity at the origin and the decay at infinity respectively.

papers.title: Quantitative periodic homogenization and uniform regularity for nonlocal equations
papers.abstract: In this work, we study quantitative homogenization for a class of nonlocal equations with periodically oscillating Hölder continuous coefficients. For Dirichlet problems in bounded $C^{1,α}$ domains, we prove $L^2$ convergence rates that are expected to be optimal. In addition, we establish interior Lipschitz estimates and optimal boundary Hölder estimates for weak solutions, with constants independent of the period of oscillation.

papers.title: Counting and Sampling Git Graphs
papers.abstract: Version Control Systems, like Git and Mercurial, represent the history of a project as a Directed Acyclic Graph, capturing divergences and merges throughout development. A widely adopted workflow, the feature branch workflow, imposes a particularly simple structure: a single main branch and features branches evolving in parallel without interfering with one another. This work presents an enumerative study of these Git graphs. We first establish a bijection between Git graphs and a simpler combinatorial class, which we term cyclariums, and derive their exact count at size n, namely \( \sum\_{k=2}^n \sum\_{f = 1}^{k-1} {k \brack f} { n - k - 1 \choose k - f - 1} \). Using a saddle-point method, we further show that this number is asymptotically equivalent to \[ \frac{e^{1/8}}{2} \left(\frac{n}{2e}\right)^{\frac n 2} \exp\left(\frac 1 2 \ln\frac n 2 \sqrt{\frac n 2} + \sqrt{2 n} + \frac{(\ln\frac n 2)^2}{32} \right) \left(\frac n 2\right)^{-3/8}. \] Additionally, we analyze the limit laws of key parameters. Finally, we address random generation by designing both a uniform sampler and a Boltzmann sampler for these graphs.

papers.title: A nilpotent version of the first Kac conjecture
papers.abstract: We derive a formula for the nilpotent Kac polynomial and define an explicit generalized Kac-Moody Lie algebra (by generators and relations) and conjecture that its graded dimensions recover the constant terms of the nilpotent Kac polynomial. We outline empirical evidence supporting the conjecture and prove it for two special classes of quivers: quivers without oriented cycles except loops and quivers with "negative enough" Euler form.

papers.title: Factorization of Elliptic Divisibility Sequences via Modular Curves
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give a structural factorization of elliptic divisibility sequences in terms of finitely many modular functions on the modular curve $X_1(N)$. More precisely, we express the functions obtained by pulling back division polynomials along the universal torsion section as products of fixed modular factors. Then we show that this factorization is compatible with the natural action of $(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})^\times$ on the modular curve $X_1(N)$ and so descends to the modular curve $X_0(N)$ via the norm map. As applications, we obtain a perfect power criterion, local and global growth estimates for the associated elliptic divisibility sequences.

papers.title: On Some Lie Group Invariant noncommutative functions
papers.abstract: We study noncommutative polynomials and functions invariant under linear actions of infinite (compact Lie) groups, with a focus on $SU(2)$ acting on two noncommuting variables. For $SU(2)$, we give a complete description of the invariant noncommutative polynomials: there are no invariants of odd degree, and in degree $2n$ the invariants are exactly the span of the $S_{2n}$-orbit of $(XY-YX)^n$. We also construct an explicit basis recursively from the operation $(A,B)\mapsto XAYB-YAXB$, and show that the space of degree-$2n$ invariants has dimension equal to the $n$-th Catalan number. All proofs proceed by direct computation with the Haar integral.

papers.title: Representations of shifted quantum affine algebras and cluster algebras II: Non simply-laced types and cluster expansions
papers.abstract: We extend our previous results on cluster structures in the Grothendieck rings of categories $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ for shifted quantum affine algebras to the non-simply laced types. We also show that, for all types, the formal power series expressions of the cluster monomials in terms of classes of positive prefundamental representations can be regarded as limits of cluster expansions, thus establishing their positivity.

papers.title: Scaling limit and universality for one-dimensional long-range first-passage metric in the linear-growth regime
papers.abstract: We prove universal Gaussian and stable fluctuation limits for one-dimensional long-range first-passage percolation with edge times $\|x-y\|^αω_{x,y}$. The positive i.i.d. weights satisfy $\mathbb{P}(ω\le t)=t^{θ+o(1)}$ as $t\downarrow0$ and $\mathbb{E}(ω^ζ)<\infty$ for some $θ,ζ>0$. For $α>1+2/θ$, the passage time $T(0,n)$ has a positive deterministic linear growth rate $μ$. For $α>1+3/θ$, we establish a Gaussian central limit theorem with linear asymptotic variance, a functional version, and limit theorems for geodesic hop and cut point counts. For $1+2/θ<α<1+3/θ$, assuming a regularly varying lower tail, we obtain a totally left-skewed stable limit with index $β=θ(α-1)-1$ and an explicit scale, together with convergence to a spectrally negative stable Lévy process in the Skorokhod $M_1$ topology. The proof constructs i.i.d. blocks between hubs through which every crossing geodesic must pass. A spread-out comparison metric makes this regeneration available for every $ζ>0$, even when the edge law has infinite mean. The key estimate identifies the exact left-tail asymptotic of the centered block reward, generated by a single fast long edge. A monotone within-block approximation yields the functional stable limit.

papers.title: Uniform parameter bounds for weighted exponential equations on simply connected domains
papers.abstract: We consider positive solutions of \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} -Δu=pλh(x)u^{p-1}\mathrm{e}^{u^p}&\text{in }Ω,\\ u>0&\text{in }Ω,\\ u=0&\text{on }\partialΩ, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $p\in[1,2]$, $λ>0$, $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ is a smooth bounded simply connected domain and $h\in C^2(\overlineΩ)$ is positive on $\overlineΩ$. The cases $p=1$ and $p=2$ correspond to the Liouville and Moser-Trudinger equations, respectively. We prove that the normalized parameter \begin{equation*} β=\frac{λp^2}{2}\left(\int_Ωh(\mathrm{e}^{u^p}-1)\mathrm{d}x\right)^{\frac{2-p}{p}}\left(\int_Ωhu^p\mathrm{e}^{u^p}\mathrm{d}x\right)^{\frac{2(p-1)}{p}} \end{equation*} is bounded by a constant depending only on $Ω$ and $h$, uniformly over all $p\in[1,2]$, $λ>0$ and positive solutions. At $p=2$, this excludes positive constrained critical points of the weighted Moser-Trudinger functional at sufficiently large Dirichlet energies. For $p=2$ and $h\equiv1$, we further prove that the energy converges uniformly to $4π$ as $λ\to0$ when $Ω$ is convex. We also develop a boundary exclusion argument for positive weights that rules out boundary blow-up for $1<p<2$ without a priori energy bound.

papers.title: Optimal path decompositions of sparse random graphs
papers.abstract: Let $\operatorname{odd}(G)$ be the number of odd-degree vertices of a graph $G$. We prove that, if $p=o(1)$ and $np/\log n\to\infty$, then with probability tending to one the random graph $G(n,p)$ has an edge decomposition into exactly $\operatorname{odd}(G)/2$ paths. This confirms a conjecture of Glock, Kühn and Osthus from 2016. The proof combines a key lemma with cycle decompositions of random graphs.

papers.title: Notes on efficient dominating sets and efficient open dominating sets in circulant graphs
papers.abstract: Let $D$ be a proper subset of $\mathbb{Z}_n$ such that $|D|$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|D|}$. We first establish a necessary and sufficient condition for $D$ to be an efficient dominating set of some circulant graph $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. Moreover, for an inverse-closed subset $S$ of $\mathbb{Z}_n\setminus\{0\}$ such that $|S|+1$ divides $n$ and is relatively prime to $\frac{n}{|S|+1}$, we give a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of efficient dominating sets in $\Cay(\mathbb{Z}_n,S)$. We also obtain some results about the set of all efficient dominating sets in any circulant graph. Similar results for efficient open dominating sets are also obtained. These results extend some theorems in [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1503--1507], [Discrete Math. 340 (2017) 1522--1527], and [Des. Codes Cryptogr. 94 (2026), 87].

papers.title: Maximal geometric quotients of flag varieties
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of maximal geometric quotient, namely a geometric quotient of a polarized pair under a torus action which has a birational contraction to any other GIT quotient. For the action of the maximal torus on a complete flag variety, we show that a maximal geometric quotient exists and it is a Mori dream space, and its Cox ring is isomorphic to the Cox ring of the flag variety. We discuss birational properties of the maximal geometric quotients, their relations with the Chow quotients and explain how to construct them for maximal torus actions on flag varieties.

papers.title: Persistent Hubs and Sharp Asymptotics in Eigenvector Preferential Attachment Trees
papers.abstract: We prove sharp almost-sure asymptotics for eigenvector preferential attachment trees in which each attachment uses eigenvector centrality with probability $α\in(0,1]$ and uniform selection with probability $1-α$. A unique persistent hub eventually has the maximum degree, which is asymptotic to $γ^2t^{2/3}$, where $γ=(9α/10)^{1/3}$. The Perron-Frobenius eigenvalue is asymptotic to $γt^{1/3}$, and the second-largest degree is asymptotic to $2γt^{1/3}$. The hub and its neighbors each carry asymptotically half of the squared Perron mass. We also identify the centrality profile by degree and an explicit mixture of geometric laws for the degree of a uniformly sampled vertex. A limiting distance profile quantifies the dandelion geometry, and vertices beyond the hub's neighbors have maximum degree of order at most $\log t$.

papers.title: The existence of the compatible lattice order on the complex field $\mathbb{C}$
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give an affirmative answer to the open question posed by G.Birkhoff and R.S.Pierce in 1956 concerning the existence of a compatible lattice order on the complex field $\mathbb{C}$. Using valuation rings theory, basis extension in infinite-dimensional vector spaces and extension of field embeddings to algebraic extensions, we obtain that for every real $t>1$ transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}$, the compatible lattice order can be chosen such that $0\prec1$, $0\vee i=t$, and $1\wedge t=0$. Consequently, $\mathbb{C}$ admits at least $2^{\aleph_0}$ distinct compatible lattice orders, each extending the usual order on $\mathbb{Q}$.

papers.title: An Anisotropic Entropy for the Rotationally Symmetric Ricci Flow
papers.abstract: For a rotationally symmetric Ricci flow $g(t)=ds^2+f(s,t)^2g_{\mathbb S^{n-1}}$, $n\ge3$, we study the scale-invariant curvature anisotropy $A=1-f_s^2+ff_{ss}$ introduced by Angenent--Knopf. At the critical power $p_*=(n-1)/(n-2)$, with $Φ=sgn(A)|A|^{p_*/2}$, we prove the distributional identity \[ (\partial_t-Δ)|A|^{p_*} =-\frac4{n-1} \left|Φ_s+(n-1)\frac{f_s}{f}Φ\right|^2. \] Integration against a conjugate heat kernel gives an anisotropic entropy formula. As an application, we obtain an entropy threshold for Type-I singularities on $\mathbb S^n$: if the entropy associated with a singular-time kernel is at most $1$ at an earlier regular time, every tangent flow at the corresponding singular point is a round shrinking sphere. This criterion follows from the $0/1$ quantization of the singular-time anisotropic density.

papers.title: Rigidity of Constant-Scalar-Curvature Ricci Shrinkers with Totally Geodesic Focal Set
papers.abstract: Let $(M^n,g,f)$ be a complete connected shrinking gradient Ricci soliton with constant scalar curvature, satisfying \[ \Ric+\nabla^2f=\frac12g. \] We prove that if the focal set of $f$ is totally geodesic, then $M$ is rigid. Equivalently, its universal cover is a product of a compact Einstein manifold and a Euclidean space.

papers.title: Finite Matrix Rings of Even Size Are Determined by Their Commuting Graphs
papers.abstract: The commuting graph of a noncommutative ring has its noncentral elements as vertices, with two distinct vertices adjacent when they commute. Akbari, Ghandehari, Hadian and Mohammadian conjectured that a full matrix ring over a finite field is determined, among rings with identity, by its commuting graph. In this paper, we prove the conjecture for every even matrix size.

papers.title: Nonlinear springs with orbits in radicals: a solvability criterion
papers.abstract: An odd polynomial oscillator has a periodic orbit given by a quadrature. When the zeros of the energy polynomial are all simple or all of even multiplicity, that quadrature is elementary exactly when the polynomial is a perfect square, and the time is a sum of inverse tangents. Recovering the displacement inverts that relation, algebraic when their coefficients are commensurate, making a closed form a Galois question. This paper identifies the group as the monodromy group of a rational map, computes its branch data from the parameters, and shows the branch value at the phase-angle singularity never vanishes, so every decomposition pairs the amplitudes reciprocally. In the commensurate family with distinct real factors, the orbit is radical exactly when the primitive inversion degree is at most four, or when reciprocal pairs leave a reduced spring of that degree. Radical orbits occur at the fifth, ninth, thirteenth and seventeenth force orders, the last only for reciprocal members, an expression recorded for each. The multiplicity hypothesis cannot be dropped. Factoring the energy polynomial into square and squarefree parts turns the quadrature into a differential of the third kind on a hyperelliptic curve, where elementarity is a torsion condition on the divisor of its poles with a vanishing holomorphic remainder. The first nonsquare elementary member appears at the ninth force order, and the power pullback inverts in closed form at every such order, giving a radical orbit for a confining spring of arbitrarily high degree with a sufficient condition for positive coefficients.

papers.title: Tumor growth models with nutrient consumption
papers.abstract: We study the saturation free boundary of the cell density and its interaction with the nutrient depletion interface in a coupled parabolic model for tumor growth with sublinear reactions. We establish a sharp quadratic--superquadratic growth dichotomy along the saturation interface and quantify the degeneration of quadratic profiles as they approach the joint saturation--depletion boundary. We further show that intrinsic regularity of the saturation interface can occur only at joint free boundary points, where half-space blow-ups of either component determine a unique joint blow-up profile. Finally, we prove a local backward coincidence between the joint and nutrient free boundaries near regular points, which yields spatial and temporal regularity of the joint interface.

papers.title: Ergodicity, memory loss, and directional stability on von Neumann algebras
papers.abstract: For a deterministic sequence of normal unital completely positive maps on a von Neumann algebra, convergence of normal states, loss of memory, and convergence of Cesàro averages are different properties. This paper separates these properties in the predual norm and identifies the precise role of composition order. Uniform loss of memory for right-appended products on the predual implies uniform convergence to a normal state without any compactness or trace assumption; the convergence rate is bounded by the image diameter. In contrast, on every infinite-dimensional $σ$-finite von Neumann algebra there are right-appended products with pointwise loss of memory but no convergent normal-state trajectory, even though all nontrivial state images equal a fixed compact line segment. Consequently, finite dimensionality is characterized by the universal implication from pointwise backward memory loss to mixing. An attained normal-functional minorization coefficient extends the common-lower-bound construction for matrix channels to arbitrary von Neumann algebras and yields quantitative contraction and unique normal entrance laws. Further results distinguish pointwise from uniform relaxation, Cesàro convergence from mixing, fixed-start from time-uniform contraction, and stationary from moving asymptotic states. As an application, inhomogeneous transfer states on spin chains, including matrix product states, are shown to have a unique thermodynamic limit, uniformly in the boundary condition, with an arbitrary von Neumann algebra as bond algebra; boundary dependence and correlations are controlled by the same product coefficients. All counterexamples are explicit and extend to algebras of types I, II, and III.

papers.title: Pooled Testing under Congestion: Operational Scaling Laws for Pool-Size Selection
papers.abstract: Classical pooled-testing rules choose pool sizes to reduce the number of tests. In practice, however, samples arrive over time, pools take time to form, testing capacity is finite, and positive pools create bursts of follow-up work. These operational features can make the test-efficient pool size far from the delay-efficient one. We formulate pooled testing with stochastic arrivals and finite testing capacity as a queueing system, and derive exact performance representations and asymptotic scaling laws for fixed-batch Dorfman testing and a dynamic two-threshold policy. The analysis reveals three distinct design regimes. When test usage is the main concern, the classical Dorfman rule is recovered and the optimal pool size scales with the inverse square root of prevalence. When delay accumulated while the laboratory is busy testing another batch matters, positive pools create service-time variability that grows more rapidly with pool size than the mean retesting burden, and the optimal scale shifts to the inverse cube root of prevalence. When waiting to assemble a pool is itself costly, the optimal fixed pool size remains bounded even as prevalence becomes very small. Under severe capacity scarcity, congestion remains relevant at the classical Dorfman scale: the square-root law survives, but with a capacity-dependent constant. Dynamic pooling separates two operational decisions that fixed pool sizes conflate. A lower threshold determines when routine testing should begin, while an upper threshold limits pooling when backlog is high. The lower threshold follows the cube-root scale, whereas the upper threshold primarily acts as congestion control. The results show how prevalence, capacity, and delay jointly determine pooling decisions and explain why operationally optimal pools can be much smaller than those suggested by test-efficiency calculations alone.

papers.title: Threshold Criteria for Bosonic and Fermionic Trimers on a Square Lattice: A Birman--Schwinger Comparison
papers.abstract: We compare two three-particle lattice models on the square lattice at total quasimomentum zero: three identical bosons with attractive contact interactions, and a two-fermion plus one distinguishable particle system with attractive interspecies contact. Using the Birman--Schwinger principle combined with symmetry reduction and strong-coupling asymptotics, we distinguish shared methodology from model-dependent spectral conclusions. For bosons, the ground-state energy behaves as minus three times the coupling plus six minus three over twice the coupling plus higher-order corrections, and exactly two bound states exist below the threshold for large coupling; the second lies at a finite distance 0.03542 below the threshold, a genuine eigenvalue rather than a threshold resonance. For fermions, the critical mass ratio is pi divided by pi minus two, approximately 2.75194; above it, a doubly degenerate level appears at strong coupling. Near onset, the binding energy follows a linear-over-logarithmic law. The results are compared with numerical finite-grid Faddeev computations and with recent three-dimensional classifications of threshold states.

papers.title: Multidimensional Infinite-Horizon Markovian Backward Stochastic Differential Equations with Continuous Coefficients and Nonzero-Sum Differential Games
papers.abstract: This paper addresses the solvability of multidimensional infinite-horizon Markovian backward stochastic differential equations with continuous coefficients. We do not require the Lipschitz property or other quantitative controls of differences, and each component of the generator is allowed to depend simultaneously on all components of the multidimensional backward variables. A local L^q-domination framework adapted to the infinite-horizon setting is developed and combined with our linear flow conjugacy analysis to obtain the required distributional control in the presence of unbounded linear drift. We also derive a common Markov representation valid for the entire family of initial states. The analytical obstacles arising from weak regularity and the multidimensional structure are thereby overcome. Furthermore, we consider a class of infinite-horizon nonzero-sum differential games with a general non linear structure, allowing player controls to be fully coupled and permitting payoff criteria that are not restricted to an exponential discount form, establish an equivalence between the game and the corresponding multidimensional infinite-horizon backward stochastic differential equations, and prove the existence of a Nash equilibrium.

papers.title: On additive bases of finite abelian groups
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group, let $p$ be the smallest prime divisor of $|G|$, and let $c_0(G)$ be the least integer $t$ such that every regular sequence over $G$ of length at least $t$ is an additive basis. Additive bases have been extensively studied in additive combinatorics, and the exact value of $c_0(G)$ has been determined for many groups of rank at least three and some groups of rank two (in which case groups of the form $C_p\oplus C_{pn}$ turn out to be exceptional). In this paper, we continue the study of $c_0(G)$ and obtain the following results. (1) Together with known results, we prove that $c_0(G)=|G|/p+p-2$ for all abelian groups $G$ with $\text{rank}(G)\geq 3$. (2) For distinct odd primes $p<q$, we determine \[ c_0(C_p\oplus C_{pq})=pq+2p-3,\qquad c_0(C_q\oplus C_{pq})=q^2+p-2. \] (3) Let $p$ be an odd prime, let $2\leq a\leq b$, and let $n$ be a positive integer with no prime divisor smaller than $p$. Then \[ c_0(C_{p^a}\oplus C_{p^bn})=p^{a+b-1}n+p-2. \] (4) For every odd integer $n\geq 3$, we prove \[ c_0(C_3\oplus C_{3n})=3n+3. \] Therefore, $c_0(G)$ is determined except possibly for groups of the form $C_p\oplus C_{pn}$ with $p\geq 5$.

papers.title: High-dimensional critical percolation and critical Branching random walks are intersection equivalent
papers.abstract: We prove that on $\mathbb Z^d$, with $d>6$, and under the usual assumption that the two-point function and the Green's function are of the same order, the probabilities to hit any finite set for a critical Branching random walk starting from the origin and the critical percolation cluster of the origin are within a positive multiplicative constant one from each other, as long as the set is sufficiently far away from the origin comparatively to its diameter. The proof relies on the introduction of a truncated equilibrium measure in percolation and the derivation of an approximate last passage formula.

papers.title: ROAR: Restricted 2-Opt And Ruin-and-recreate Heuristic for Large and Extreme Scale Traveling Repairman Problem
papers.abstract: The Traveling Repairman Problem minimizes cumulative arrival times rather than the total route length, as in the classical Traveling Salesman Problem. The literature contains several legacy metaheuristics for the TRP; however, most are evaluated on small- and medium-scale instances and show limited scalability for large and extreme datasets. GILS-RVND, the current gold standard in metaheuristic algorithms, performs well on small and medium instances but struggles to scale due to the exhaustive neighborhood search in the RVND phase. To address this limitation, we introduce Restricted 2-Opt And Ruin-and-recreate (ROAR), a Large Neighborhood Search-based method that integrates ruin-and-recreate with greedy insertion and a restricted, insertion-anchored 2-opt operator. Computational experiments demonstrate that ROAR produces high-quality solutions for large-scale instances and outperforms existing methods under strict time limits. We further introduce an O(1)-time, O(1)-space algorithm for evaluating 2-opt moves during a contiguous systematic sweep, which, to the best of our knowledge, is unprecedented. Finally, we evaluate ROAR on instances with up to 200,000 nodes, substantially exceeding the largest instances previously reported in the literature (11,849 nodes).

papers.title: Enumeration of zero-sum subsequences: A proof of Bialostocki-Lotspeich conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n\ge 2$, and let $S=g_1\cdot\ldots\cdot g_{\ell}$ be a sequence over $C_n$, with repetitions allowed. We denote by $\mathsf N_0^n(S)$ the number of subsets $I\subseteq[1,\ell]$ with $|I|=n$ and $\sum_{i\in I}g_i=0$. A conjecture proposed by Bialostocki and Lotspeich in 1992 states that $$\mathsf N_0^n(S)\ge \binom{\lfloor |S|/2\rfloor}{n}+ \binom{\lceil |S|/2\rceil}{n}.$$ Several partial results toward this conjecture are known. In this paper, we prove this conjecture completely.

papers.title: Fractal transference principle for conformal iterated function systems
papers.abstract: We establish a complex one-dimensional fractal transference principle connecting density combinatorics with the fractal geometry of complex continued fractions. Our framework applies to a broad class of conformal iterated function systems indexed by lattice points, including those associated with the Hurwitz continued fraction, and transfers positive-density combinatorial patterns to digit sets while preserving the maximal Hausdorff dimension. As applications, we obtain fractal counterparts of the multidimensional and polynomial Szemerédi theorems, as well as their relativized versions yielding a counterpart of the multidimensional Green--Tao theorem.

papers.title: Spectral delocalization and central limit theorems for Fourier functionals of stationary Gaussian fields
papers.abstract: We characterize Gaussian fluctuations of Fourier-Hermite functionals of stationary Gaussian fields on locally compact Abelian groups via spectral delocalization: conditional on the total spectral sum being near the probed frequency, no partial sum concentrates. Under suitable assumptions, this reduces Gaussian convergence to small-ball estimates for convolution powers of the spectral measure, without model-specific contraction estimates. On $\mathbb T^d$, the criterion yields CLTs at every fixed frequency for band-limited fields and random trigonometric polynomials, and extends the known failure of Gaussian convergence for planar arithmetic random waves from the fourth chaos to all even orders $q\ge4$. On $\mathbb R^d$ and $\mathbb Z^d$, we establish a Breuer-Major theorem for Fourier functionals at every frequency with nonzero limiting variance. Cyclical long-memory models exhibit frequency-dependent Gaussian convergence. We also establish CLTs and variance asymptotics for singular continuous spectral measures, including those of stationary Gaussian solutions of linear PDEs. At zero frequency, weak Ahlfors regularity of the spectral support and an $L^2$ density suffice for second-chaos CLTs, covering fractal sets, the Airy surface of Gaussian sea waves, and smooth compact manifolds. For a class of smooth hypersurfaces, we obtain the same variance rates and CLTs known for classical nonlinear functionals of Berry's random wave model. Finally, for random waves with spherical spectral densities bounded above and below, we classify Gaussian convergence at every frequency $\|z\|\le q$: it fails only for the planar second chaos when $0<\|z\|<2$.

papers.title: Finite $\mathbf{BM}$-algebras and fixed-point combinators
papers.abstract: We study algebras for the $\mathbf{BM}$-, $\mathbf{BI}$-, and $\mathbf{BMI}$-fragments of combinatory logic, where $\mathbf{B} xyz \to_{w} x\left(yz\right)$, $\mathbf{M} x \to_{w} xx$ and $\mathbf{I} x \to_{w} x$. We prove that every finite $\mathbf{BM}$-algebra $\mathcal{A}$ contains an element $Y$ satisfying $Yx = x\left(Yx\right)$ for all $x\in A$. Moreover, a single closed $\mathbf{BM}$-term represents such an element in every finite $\mathbf{BM}$-algebra. On the other hand, we show that there exists an infinite $\mathbf{BMI}$-algebra with no such element. Consequently, the variety of $\mathbf{BM}$-algebras is not generated by finite $\mathbf{BM}$-algebras. We also characterise finite $\mathbf{BI}$-algebras as finite semigroups with two distinguished left units $B$ and $I$, and finite $\mathbf{BMI}$-algebras as finite idempotent semigroups with three distinguished left units $B$, $M$ and $I$.

papers.title: New inhomogeneous Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds with large symmetry group
papers.abstract: We study compact non-Kähler Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds whose connected full group of holomorphic isometries acts with cohomogeneity one. We prove that the Lie algebra of this group is isomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^3\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$ or $\mathbb{R}^2\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$, unless the Bismut connection is flat. We then focus on the first case, where we determine the possible singular isotropy algebras and reduce the Bismut Hermitian-Einstein condition to a system of ordinary differential equations. We obtain explicit solutions satisfying suitable smoothness conditions, that yield families of compact and complete non-compact non-Kähler Bismut Hermitian-Einstein threefolds with non-constant scalar curvature and non-zero Bismut curvature, including examples on $S^3\times S^3$ and $S^3\times S^1\times\mathbb{R}^2$, respectively. We also investigate the topology of the compact examples and determine the asymptotic scalar curvature of the non-compact ones. Moreover, we prove the existence of a smooth deformation of a Bismut-flat Samelson structure on $S^3\times S^3$ through non-Kähler Bismut Hermitian-Einstein structures that are not Bismut-flat. The regularity of the constructed compact examples is also investigated.

papers.title: Operator Barron Regularity for Elliptic Equations and Application to Neural Operator Approximation
papers.abstract: We develop a spectral Barron regularity framework for nonlinear operators between infinite-dimensional function spaces. Using Hilbert-valued Fourier representations of finite-dimensional input truncations, we establish bounds that are uniform in the input truncation dimension and prove arbitrary-order Barron regularity for a class of elliptic solution operators. Second, we use this operator Barron regularity to derive approximation error bounds for an FNO-type neural operator, with explicit dependence on the input truncation dimension, output reconstruction dimension, and network width. For a fixed input truncation dimension, optimizing the neural approximation bound over the Barron regularity order yields stretched-exponential decay of the approximation error in the network width. We also show some numerical experiments to support the predicted rate.

papers.title: A Two-Stage Optimization Framework for Real-World Large-Scale University Course Timetabling Based on Orthogonalized Hierarchical Modeling and Conflict-Driven ALNS Repair
papers.abstract: University course timetabling is a large-scale combinatorial optimization problem involving strongly coupled temporal and resource constraints. This paper proposes a two-stage optimization framework for real-world large-scale university course timetabling, integrating orthogonalized hierarchical modeling with conflict-driven adaptive large neighborhood search (ALNS) repair. The first stage performs global course-level optimization, while the second identifies residual conflicts through a conflict graph and localizes them into connected conflict regions. The Course--Occurrence--Session representation provides the structural basis for multi-granularity repair, which employs Cluster-, Course-, Occurrence-, and Session-level destroy operators within the ALNS framework, followed by fine-grained greedy repair. The framework is evaluated on a real-world university timetabling instance involving 3,073 course groups, 8,015 scheduling events, 998 student classes, and 1,511 instructors. Ablation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of hierarchical repair granularity and adaptive operator selection. Across ten independent runs, the ALNS + Greedy framework achieves a mean residual conflict count of 18.50, compared with 172 for deterministic Greedy-only repair under the same initial scheduling conditions, representing an 89.24\% reduction. These results support the effectiveness of the proposed conflict-driven hierarchical repair framework for large-scale university course timetabling.

papers.title: Large-bulk-viscosity limit for two-dimensional compressible micropolar fluids with vacuum
papers.abstract: We consider the Cauchy problem for the two-dimensional compressible micropolar fluid system on the torus $\mathbb T^2$. The initial density is bounded and nonnegative and may contain vacuum, while the initial velocity and microrotation belong to $H^1(\mathbb T^2)$. For sufficiently large bulk viscosity $ν$, we prove the global-in-time existence of solutions without a smallness assumption on the $H^1$ size of the data, provided that the initial compressible component is well prepared in the sense that $\sqrtν\|\operatorname{div}u_0\|_{L^2}$ is uniformly bounded. The proof combines the effective viscous flux with a coupled energy scheme that exploits the vorticity--microrotation dissipation at both the basic and material-derivative levels. For the linear pressure law, we also prove uniqueness in the stated solution class by means of a coupled backward parabolic problem, logarithmic interpolation, and Osgood's lemma. For fixed initial data with $\operatorname{div}u_0=0$, we also justify the limit $ν\to\infty$: every sequence of the corresponding solutions admits a subsequence converging to a solution of the two-dimensional inhomogeneous incompressible micropolar system.

papers.title: Quantum Fisher Information Deficit as a Geometric Signature of Strong-to-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking
papers.abstract: Recently, strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) has been established as a framework for describing quantum phases in open systems. However SW-SSB cannot be characterized by conventional charged two-point correlators. In this work, we show that, for strongly $\mathbb{Z}_2$-symmetric states with local charged involutions, SW-SSB manifests as a persistent deficit from the maximal quantum Fisher information (QFI) under symmetry-neutral pair rotations. A model-independent inequality hierarchy establishes the equivalence of this deficit with fidelity and Rényi-1 correlators as asymptotic long-range-order diagnostics. It thereby connects finite-angle state overlaps to a constraint on the infinitesimal Bures geometry along the same pair-generated orbit. For symmetry-projected Gibbs states, we further derive a lower bound on the deficit governed by the mean energy injected by the pair operation. Crucially, locality keeps this energy cost uniformly bounded in system size and endpoint separation, maintaining a finite gap below the maximal QFI at any fixed finite temperature. When ordinary charged long range order is absent, this persistent geometric constraint provides a quantitative information-geometric characterization of thermal SW-SSB.

papers.title: Exact decoherence dynamics of a detector coupled to vacuum fluctuations in bounded geometries
papers.abstract: The properties of quantum vacuum are highly sensitive to the underlying spacetime geometry and boundary conditions. We investigate in this paper the decoherence dynamics of a two-level system (detector) coupled to a vacuum scalar field through the $\hatσ_z$-coupling scheme under various boundary environments. By rigorously evaluating the reduced density matrix of the detector, we derive an exact general expression for the detector's decoherence function, $γ(Δt)$, and use it to characterize the dynamical decoherence of a detector in three scenarios: free space, a perfectly reflecting boundary, and a cavity formed by two parallel reflecting boundaries. We find that in free space the detector's coherence decays monotonically with time, indicating that vacuum fluctuations alone inevitably lead to a complete loss of coherence. In the single-boundary case, by contrast, the detector's coherence displays non-monotonic time evolution: $γ(Δt)$ increases with time up to a maximum and then settles to a steady value, indicating that the initial coherence can be partially preserved due to the presence of the boundary. When the detector is placed inside a cavity, its coherence evolution exhibits oscillatory behavior, and a significant fraction of the initial coherence survives. Moreover, for the same detector-boundary distance, more coherence is preserved in the cavity case than in the single-boundary case. These results provide a viable route for engineering quantum coherence via boundary conditions.

papers.title: Reducing Complexity of Pseudo-Marginal Sequential Monte Carlo via Hierarchical Tempering
papers.abstract: The Bayesian approach to inverse problems provides a powerful framework for inferring unknown parameters from noisy observations. Among the computationally most challenging statistical inference problems are problems with intractable likelihoods, especially if no unbiased likelihood estimator is available. We focus on a class of such problems, where a biased likelihood estimator is obtained through a stochastic approximation of a forward map (stochastic solver). Obtaining an empirical posterior approximation in applications is very expensive due to the repeated stochastic solver evaluations required by standard sampling methods. To address this computational bottleneck, we develop a novel algorithm based on a density-tempered marginalized Sequential Monte Carlo (SMC) sampler. Our approach (hierarchical SMC) accelerates inference by leveraging a hierarchy of stochastic solvers with increasing accuracy both along the tempering sequence and within mutation stages of the SMC sampler. We establish, under additional assumptions, that the asymptotic speedup is proportional to the number of tempering stages $T$. We demonstrate computational gains on several examples, including a nonlinear, high-contrast inverse problem arising in photoacoustic medical imaging. On this problem, we demonstrate a speedup by a factor of 14.3, reducing the inference wall-clock time from about 4.6 days to 7.7 hours on an NVIDIA A40 GPU.

papers.title: Global Well-Posedness and Large Time Asymptotic Behavior of Strong Solutions to the Compressible Viscous Non-Resistive MHD Equations with Vacuum
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider the Cauchy problem to the compressible viscous non-resistive magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) system in $\mathbb{R}^3$, in which the velocity is planar while the magnetic field is vertical. For regular initial data with small energy but possibly large oscillations, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solution with vacuum. In addition, the large-time behavior of the solution is investigated. A key ingredient is an application of the Bourgain--Brezis divergence estimate to handle the total pressure $ρ^γ+m^2$ for any adiabatic index $γ>1$. This enables us to control both components of the total pressure, $ρ^γ$ and $m^2$, by a single estimate that remains valid in the presence of vacuum. To the best of our knowledge, our result is the first one on global solvability to the compressible, viscous, non-resistive MHD system in the special 2$\frac12$-dimensional whole space allowing vacuum.

papers.title: Global well-posedness and scattering of energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on high-dimensional hyperbolic spaces
papers.abstract: We prove global well-posedness and scattering for the energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} i\partial_t u + Δu = |u|^{\frac{4}{d-2}} u, u(0) = u_0, \end{cases} \end{equation*} on hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^d(d \geq 4)$. We mainly utilize the concentration-compactness/rigidity method. We establish a linear profile decomposition on high-dimensional hyperbolic spaces and prove that the nonlinear profile on hyperbolic spaces can be approximated by the solutions of the energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on Euclidean spaces, then obtaining the global well-posedness and scattering of the energy-critical defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation on the high-dimensional hyperbolic space.

papers.title: The NWU ageing property of the gamma-gamma distribution
papers.abstract: Baricz et al. [BPV2011] posed the question of whether the $K$-distribution (or gamma-gamma distribution) satisfies the ageing property known as the new is better than used (NBU) property. In this paper we address this question by establishing that, under certain parameter conditions, the gamma-gamma distribution satisfies the new is worse than used (NWU) property rather than the NBU property. For the remaining parameter ranges, we show that the gamma-gamma distribution is neither NBU nor NWU. The proofs rely on tools from the theory of stochastic orders of random variables. Moreover, by exploiting the fact that the random variable that follows the $K$-distribution is actually the product of two independent gamma random variables, we obtain alternative proofs of our results. Similarly, by exploiting the fact that the random variable that follows the beta-prime distribution is actually the quotient of two independent gamma random variables, we establish analogous NBU/NWU properties for this distribution. We also establish sufficient conditions under which the product of two independent positive random variables possesses the NWU and decreasing failure rate (DFR) properties. On the other hand, we show that the survival function of the $K$-distribution is hyperbolically completely monotone by representing it as the Laplace transform of a random variable belonging to the class of generalized gamma convolutions. As a consequence, we establish some monotonicity properties of the Mills ratio and hazard rate function of the $K$-distribution. These results provide further insight into the ageing and monotonicity properties of the gamma-gamma distribution. In addition, we derive a new integral representation and two new series representations, as well as bounds, for the survival function of the $K$-distribution.

papers.title: All Strict Calabi--Yau Threefolds of Height One Lift to Characteristic 0
papers.abstract: We prove that every strict Calabi--Yau threefold of Artin--Mazur height one over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0 admits a projective lift to W(k). No assumption is made on the torsion in its crystalline cohomology, and p is arbitrary. Using the crystalline period map of Brantner and Taelman, we show that the obstruction to extending a lift over W_n(k) is the Bockstein of a torsion coordinate of its period point, and that this coordinate can always be made to vanish by varying the lift. The mixed-characteristic deformation functor need not be smooth: for a Calabi--Yau threefold of height one constructed by Addington and Bragg in characteristic 3, some lifts over W_2(k) do not extend over W_3(k). This disproves a conjecture of Achinger and Zdanowicz.

papers.title: Observer-Based Event-Triggered Control of Infinite-Dimensional Linear Systems
papers.abstract: We investigate observer-based event-triggered stabilization of infinite-dimensional linear systems, such as those governed by partial differential equations. A Luenberger observer and a feedback gain are assumed to stabilize the closed loop in continuous time, and we study what happens when the control input is only updated at instants generated by a dynamic event-triggering mechanism. Unlike approaches that rely on state-dependent triggering rules, our condition only involves the observer state and the measured output, which makes it implementable when the full state is not measured. It compares the deviation of a monitored signal of the observer since the last update with a threshold made of two parts. The first one is a relative part, proportional to the current size of this signal, and the second one is a positive internal variable, which does not depend on the observer state. In particular, the case where the threshold reduces to the internal variable alone is covered. Under suitable assumptions, we establish the well-posedness of the closed-loop system and the absence of Zeno behavior for general choices of these two parts, and we prove its exponential stability under a small-gain condition on the relative part. We further analyse the existence of a dwell-time, namely a positive lower bound on the time elapsed between two consecutive triggering instants. When the sampled dynamics is bounded, as in finite-dimensional systems or systems with a finite-dimensional unstable part, we obtain a dwell-time independent of the initial data, together with exponential stability. For unbounded generators, we exhibit a system satisfying all our assumptions for which no triggering rule can achieve both a dwell-time independent of the initial data and bounded trajectories.

papers.title: Improved Brunn--Minkowski inequality for $θ$-convolution bodies
papers.abstract: For $n\geq 2$, we study the optimal function $\varphi_n$ in the Brunn-Minkowski inequality for $θ$-convolution bodies $|K+_θL|^{1/n}\geq\varphi_n(θ)(|K|^{1/n}+|L|^{1/n})$ for any convex bodies $K,L\subset\mathbb{R}^n$. We improve the known lower bound for every $0<θ<(3/4)^n$ and determine $\varphi_n$ on an interval strictly containing $[(2/3)^n,1]$. For $θ<1$ in this interval, equality holds if and only if $K$ and $-L$ are translates of the same $n$-dimensional simplex. The proof reduces the geometric problem to a sharp one-dimensional estimate for nonnegative concave functions under a weighted integral constraint.

papers.title: Moment Polyptychs and the Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties
papers.abstract: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric variety of complex dimension $2n$ using symplectic cutting. When the defining arrangement is cooriented so that its base region is non-empty and bounded, fibre rotation has proper moment map and produces compact Kähler orbifold cuts carrying the residual torus action. We introduce the moment polyptych of such a cut, a polytopal complex assembled from truncated arrangement regions, and show that its vertices and local lattice data determine the fixed points, tangent weights, and finite orbifold groups required for equivariant orbifold Riemann-Roch localisation. Even for a smooth hypertoric manifold, a reducible core forces every cut in the outer cut chamber to have non-trivial cyclic isotropy, while the cuts are smooth if and only if the manifold is the cotangent bundle of its distinguished compact toric subvariety, which is then a product of projective spaces. For a positive regular integral level $d$ in the outer cut chamber, algebraic cutting identifies the cut's quantisation with a finite filtration piece of the circle-graded quantisation of the original hypertoric variety, whose successive quotients recover the individual circle-weight spaces. We prove that the higher cohomology of the pre-quantum line orbibundle vanishes at every such level, so that the localised index is the character of the actual space of sections. Finally, a residual weight $x$ occurs at level $d$ if and only if $\mathcal{S}(x) \leq d$, where $\mathcal{S}$ is the arrangement slack function, with multiplicity $\binom{d - \mathcal{S}(x) + n}{n}$. Thus, each finite stage admits a weighted lattice-point description whose multiplicity function is supported on the lattice points in the support of the level-$d$ moment polyptych.

papers.title: GKS Fully Homomorphic Encryption: Security Analysis
papers.abstract: All traditional encryption schemes share a fundamental operational vulnerability: encrypted data must be decrypted before it can be used. Fully homomorphic encryption eliminates this vulnerability by enabling computation directly on encrypted data, but existing FHE schemes impose substantial practical constraints that limit deployment. This paper presents a formal security analysis of the Gribov-Kahrobaei-Shpilrain (GKS) private-key FHE scheme. GKS requires no bootstrapping or de-linearization, produces bit-exact decryption, supports native encrypted search, and scales to unbounded depth.

papers.title: A hyper-reduction strategy for elastoplastic hydro-mechanical problems in partially saturated soil
papers.abstract: This work proposes a hyper-reduced order model for coupled hydro-mechanical simulations of elastoplastic deformation and water flow in partially saturated soils. These simulations are used to monitor and assess the safety of geotechnical structures such as earthfill dams, where calibration, uncertainty quantification and scenario analysis require solving the same transient model many times for different parameter values. The displacement and the pore pressure are approximated in a field-split reduced basis obtained by proper orthogonal decomposition, and the Galerkin-projected equations are integrated with decomposed cubature rules, one per balance equation, built with the energy-conserving sampling and weighting (ECSW) method. Each residual is split into an affine part and a nonlinear correction: the affine part is computed exactly, at negligible online cost, so that the cubature rule only needs to approximate the correction, which is localized in space. The construction is independent of the constitutive model choices and is implemented in FEniCSx by assembling the original variational forms on the small set of elements selected by ECSW. The method is tested on two- and three-dimensional dams retaining tailings and water, simulating a raise of the dam and the subsequent consolidation phase, with the friction angle, stiffness and hydraulic conductivity of the dam material and the height of the raise as varying parameters. The hyper-reduced model reproduces the displacement and pressure fields with errors below $0.5\%$ with respect to the finite element solution, achieving speed-ups of up to $43\times$ in two dimensions and $77\times$ in three. These performance gains grow with the extent of the plastic yielding, and the selected elements concentrate in the plastified and unsaturated zones, whose size is set by the physics rather than by the mesh resolution.

papers.title: Jacob's ladders and wander from Hardy-Littlewood integral (1918) to the $ζ$-Platonic cube form of equivalent of the Fermat-Wiles theorem
papers.abstract: In this paper we obtain $ζ$-Platonic cube form of our almost linear formula. From this follows, for example, the $ζ$-Platonic equivalent of the Fermat-Wiles theorem. The last result represents the point of contact between the Hardy-Littlewood integral and the Fermat-Wiles theorem and also with one of the Platonic solid - cube.

papers.title: Three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations
papers.abstract: We show that if a three-manifold $M$ admits a veering triangulation, then the dual spine of every essential triangulation of $M$ can be smoothed to a branched surface. We use this criterion to identify a large collection of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations. We then use the same criterion to construct the first infinite family of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds without veering triangulations.

papers.title: A sparse canonical Rado theorem
papers.abstract: Canonical Ramsey theory studies structured colour patterns in colourings with arbitrarily many colours. Lefmann's canonical Rado theorem extends the canonical van der Waerden theorem of Erdős and Graham to partition-regular linear systems. Recently, Alvarado, Kohayakawa, Morris, Mota and Ortega proved a sparse canonical van der Waerden theorem for random set $[n]_p$. In this paper, we prove a sparse canonical Rado theorem. For every irredundant partition-regular matrix $A$ of positive rank with $k\ge3$ columns, and every prescribed partition witnessing the columns condition, if $p\ge Cn^{-1/m(A)}$, then with probability at least $1-e^{-cnp}$ every colouring of $[n]_p$ contains $$Ω\big(p^k n^{k-\rank(A)}\big)$$ canonical solutions of $A\mathbf x=0$ with distinct coordinates. A matching 0-statement holds when the prescribed partition has one or at least three blocks; the Schur equation shows that it can fail for two-block patterns. For every prescribed partition, we also establish a robust threshold at the same scale under deletion of a fixed positive proportion of the random set.

papers.title: Relative derived delooping levels and torsion intervals
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a support $τ$-tilting module over a finite dimensional algebra $A$, and let $\mathcal{V}\subseteq \text{Fac}U$ be any torsion class. The heart $\mathcal H=\text{Fac} U\cap \mathcal{V}^\perp$ inherits the exact structure from mod$A$ and admits an Ext-progenerator $P$. Let $B=\text{End}_A(P)$. We define the relative derived delooping level on the exact heart $\mathcal H$ and compare it with the relative delooping level on $\mathcal {H}$ and the derived delooping level of $B$. We show that $\text{Findim} B^{op}$ is bounded by the relative derived delooping level on the $\mathcal H$. For a wide heart, the relative derived delooping level on the heart equals the derived delooping level of $B$. We obtain explicit bounds from representation-finite relative syzygy strata and characterize global first-order finiteness using an Ext-injective cogenerator.

papers.title: On $π$-nilpotencies of finite skew braces
papers.abstract: Let $π$ be a set of primes. We extend the theory of left and right $π$-nilpotency in skew braces beyond the nilpotent type setting, and introduce the study of central $π$-nilpotency for finite skew braces. We investigate the relationships between these three notions, and a characterisation of central $π$-nilpotency in terms of chief factors is also established. This leads to the introduction of the $π$-Fitting ideal of a skew brace, for which we prove a local analogue of Fitting's theorem and provide a description in terms of centralisers of chief factors. Finally, we introduce the $π$-core of a skew brace and investigate its relationship with $π$-ideals and central $π$-nilpotency.

papers.title: Quantum Annealing for Gamma-ray Source Detection and Localization with AGILE Data
papers.abstract: The detection and localization of gamma-ray sources via maximum-likelihood analysis is a complex parameter optimization problem. We address this challenge using quantum annealing, a computational approach that solves optimization tasks by encoding them into the ground state of an Ising Hamiltonian. Specifically, we apply this method to observations from AGILE's Gamma-Ray Imaging Detector (GRID) in the 30 MeV-50 GeV band. We reformulated the standard analysis as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem. We tested this method on a set of AGILE observations generated with AGILEpy, solving the QUBO with simulated quantum annealing. The method reproduces the classical flux and position estimates within their statistical uncertainty and identifies the correct grid node among the candidate positions in 97% of the maps. These promising results demonstrate that quantum annealing could be used in this optimization problem, laying the ground for its deployment on actual quantum annealers.

papers.title: The Beurling-type theorem for powers of weighted Bergman shifts
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal{B}_α$ denote the shift operator on the weighted Bergman space $A^2_α(\mathbb{D})$. We prove that, for every integer $k\geq1$, the Beurling-type theorem holds for $\mathcal{B}_α^k$ on $A^2_α(\mathbb{D})$ if and only if $-1<α\leq1$. We also show that, for every $α>-1$, there exists a finite Blaschke product $B$ such that $M_{B}$ admits a cyclic invariant subspace but fails the wandering subspace property.

papers.title: Bridgeland stability and Gieseker stability I: Limit stability
papers.abstract: We study the large volume limit of Bridgeland stability conditions on smooth projective varieties. For each fixed ray in a suitable angular sector, we prove that an object of $\mathrm{D}^b(X)$ is Bridgeland (semi)stable in the corresponding hearts for all sufficiently large radii if and only if it is a pure $H$-Gieseker (semi)stable sheaf. In this sector, we identify the category of coherent sheaves as the limiting heart in the sense of eventual membership. We also identify a perverse coherent limiting heart in the opposite angular sector. The key ingredients are uniform HN-phase estimates for bounded families of pure sheaves, coefficient bounds for the coherent images of potential destabilizers, and a criterion forcing narrow exact sequences in the varying hearts to be bounded saturated coherent sequences.

papers.title: On δ-derivations of \mathfrak{saff}_{n+1}
papers.abstract: We study $δ$-derivations of the finite-dimensional perfect Lie algebra $\mathfrak{saff}_{n+1}=\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})\ltimes\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$, where $\mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ is the natural $\mathfrak{sl}_{n+1}(\mathbb{C})$-module. For $n>1$ and $δ\ne1$, we prove that every nonzero $δ$-derivation occurs at $δ=\frac12$ and is a scalar multiple of the identity. For $n=1$, we explicitly describe the four-dimensional space of $(-2)$-derivations.

papers.title: Separation Theorems for Increasing Convex and Weak 3-Convex Orders on Real-Valued Random Variables
papers.abstract: We examine separation theorems for the increasing convex (stop-loss) order and weak 3-convex order. We improve prior proofs for the increasing convex order by using integrated survival functions. We extend the separation theorem for weak 3-convex order from non-negative random variables to general real-valued random variables with finite second moments via a constructive approach based on higher-order integrated survival functions. A counterexample verifies that the $3$-convex order and $2$-convex order chain does not hold for the weak $3$-convex order. Our results enrich stochastic order theories for actuarial science and risk management.

papers.title: From amplituhedra to flagtopes
papers.abstract: The amplituhedron was introduced by Arkani-Hamed and Trnka (2014) to geometrically encode scattering amplitudes in high-energy physics. It can be viewed as the generalization of a cyclic polytope into the Grassmannian, and is defined to be the projection of the totally nonnegative part of one Grassmannian with respect to a totally negative element of a second Grassmannian. We construct a Lie-theoretic generalization of amplituhedra called 'flag amplituhedra', by replacing the pair of Grassmannians in the definition with an arbitrary pair of partial flag varieties for a reductive group $G$. We study in detail an example of a flag amplituhedron which is not a Grassmannian amplituhedron; it is a curved hexagon in $\mathbb{P}^1\times \mathbb{P}^1$.

papers.title: Finite Tensor 2-Categories
papers.abstract: We propose a definition of a finite linear 2-category, as a 2-categorical analogue of the notion of a finite abelian category of Etingof-Ostrik. We go on to prove that finite linear 2-categories with adjunctible projectives are precisely the Morita 2-categories of (all) algebras in a finite multitensor category. Thus, finite linear 2-categories with adjunctible projectives can be viewed as `non-semisimple' generalizations of the finite semisimple 2-categories of Douglas-Reutter. Secondly, we study finite multitensor 2-categories, that is, finite linear 2-categories equipped with a monoidal structure for which every objects has duals. We extend several results about fusion 2-categories to our present setting. In particular, we investigate the properties of the 2-category of bimodules over a rigid algebra $\mathcal{A}$ in a finite tensor 2-category $\mathfrak{C}$. We show that, if $\mathfrak{C}$ has adjunctible projectives, then the 2-category of $\mathcal{A}$-$\mathcal{A}$-bimodules in $\mathfrak{C}$ is a finite multitensor 2-category. This construction provides many examples of finite tensor 2-categories. For instance, the Drinfeld center of a finite tensor 2-category with adjunctible projectives is a finite tensor 2-category.

papers.title: RePAIR: Inverting Backdoor Attacks in Semantic Segmentation
papers.abstract: Despite significant advances in computer vision, semantic segmentation models remain vulnerable to backdoor attacks, posing a security risk. These attacks redirect pixels of a chosen victim class to an attacker-specified target class when a trigger is present, while preserving clean predictions. Existing defenses are largely derived from image classification, while dedicated segmentation defenses remain scarce and typically require retraining or model modification. We introduce RePAIR, a post-hoc, label-free, attack-unaware defense based on the observation that backdoor-induced shifts can be stronger in the classifier head than in internal representations, leaving recoverable victim-class semantics. RePAIR infers the victim-target relation from an unlabeled, potentially contaminated image pool, constructs a safety-approved semantic reference, and localizes suspicious pixels by comparing head predictions with internal semantic evidence. It then applies feature-space and output corrections toward the inferred victim semantics, while conservative localization and output constraints limit changes to benign predictions. We model the attack as adversarial probability transport and repair as its approximate reversal, deriving bounds and sufficient conditions for localization, residual attack success, clean-side changes, defense-induced target predictions, and attack-unaware pair identification. Experiments across segmentation architectures and attack settings show that RePAIR substantially reduces attack success while largely preserving clean performance.

papers.title: Extended stability timescales for the 2D3C rotating stratified Boussinesq equations
papers.abstract: We study the time evolution of a vertical-slice model for incompressible inhomogeneous rotating fluids perturbed around a stably stratified rest state with linear buoyancy profile. For $\varepsilon$-small localized initial data with vanishing potential vorticity, we prove that solutions remain of size $O(\varepsilon)$ up to times of order $\varepsilon^{-\frac43}$, and up to times of order $\varepsilon^{-2}$ in a regime where the Brunt--Väisälä frequency and the Coriolis parameter are comparable. The first result relies on linear dispersion with amplitude decay rate $\langle t\rangle^{-\frac12}$, while the second exploits the absence of three-wave resonances via a normal form transformation. Our results remain valid for small nonzero initial potential vorticity, whose size is propagated by means of an intrinsic change of coordinates.

papers.title: The TEMPO network can be made independent of the system size
papers.abstract: The time-evolving matrix product operator (TEMPO) method efficiently simulates non-Markovian open quantum system dynamics by contracting a two-dimensional tensor network representing the time-discretized Feynman-Vernon influence functional. The standard form of this network has an unfavorable scaling with the size of the system. We show that, within the usual second-order time-step error, the dimensions of all internal network bonds can be reduced to $(2m+1)(m+1)$, where $m$ is the number of independent coupling channels. This dimension does not depend on the number of distinct eigenvalues of the coupling operators. The system size only enters in the final boundary layer of the network, making large system sizes accessible to TEMPO methods. This structure was discovered by Claude Opus 5.5 during guided algorithm development.

papers.title: Resolving a Problem of Lv and Koolen on the Smallest Eigenvalue of Distance-Regular Graphs
papers.abstract: Let $Γ$ be a distance-regular graph with valency $k$, diameter $D\ge3$, and eigenvalues $k=θ_0>θ_1>\cdots>θ_D$. Put $b\coloneqq b_1/(θ_1+1)$, and let $1=u_0>u_1>\cdots>u_D$ be the standard sequence associated with $θ_1$. Lv and Koolen asked whether the negative of the smallest eigenvalue of a distance-regular graph can be bounded above in terms of its diameter $D$ and the parameter $b$ alone. In this paper, we answer this question affirmatively by proving that $-θ_D\le\prod_{i=2}^D(1-u_i)/(u_1-u_i) <(b+1)^{D-1}$. Equality in the product bound holds if and only if $Γ$ is $Q$-polynomial with respect to the primitive idempotent corresponding to $θ_1$. For every integer $D\ge4$, we further establish the explicit bound $-θ_D\le b^{D-1}+b^{D-2} +\frac{27}{2}(D-2)b^{D-3}$ whenever $b\ge\max\{8,\sqrt{12(D-2)}\}$. Both leading coefficients are best possible for each fixed $D\ge4$. The proof uses a spectral product theorem of Micchelli and Willoughby applied to Schur multiplication in the Bose--Mesner algebra.

papers.title: Klt varieties with semipositive anticanonical bundle : symmetric tensors, holonomy and structure
papers.abstract: The aim of this article is to study klt projective varieties such that the anticanonical bundle is semipositive from the differential-geometric point of view. The study of the holonomy of such varieties yields generalizations of several results. We show that the dimension of the space of symmetric differentials is bounded by a constant depending on the augmented irregularity, generalizing a result of Kobayashi. If we endow such a variety $X$ with a metric $ω$ whose Ricci curvature is non-negative, then we show that the holonomy of the regular locus is compact. If we assume that $X$ has canonical singularities, then we show that the general fiber of the Albanese map can be decomposed into a product of irreducible Calabi-Yau varieties, irreducible holomorphic symplectic varieties and hereditarily rationally connected varieties by the holonomy generalizing a structure theorem of Campana, Demailly and Peternell. To conclude, we show that the fundamental group of the regular locus of such varieties is virtually abelian.

papers.title: Quantitative Rigidity of Ricci Nonnegative Manifolds via the Regular Green Constant
papers.abstract: For a Ricci non-negative non-parabolic manifold $(M^{n\ge3},g)$, assuming the minimal normalized Green function admits the asymptotic expansion $G=r^{2-n}+H_p+O_1(r)$, we prove the scaling invariant defect $H_pR^{n-2}$ controls the geometry of the geodesic ball quantitatively, $\frac{1}{R}d_{GH}(B_p(R),B_0^{\mathbb{R}^n}(R))\le C_n \left(H_p R^{n-2}\right)^{\frac{1}{88(n+1)(4n+1)}}$.

papers.title: Factorizations by column blocks and Schubert polynomials as products of key polynomials
papers.abstract: We classify the Schubert polynomials that are products of key polynomials and explicitly determine their finest key factorization. Their indexing permutations are precisely those avoiding ten classical patterns of length six, which form the minimal pattern basis. More generally, the connected components of the column interaction graph give the unique finest factorization of a dual flagged Weyl character into nonconstant diagram characters. Every other such factorization is obtained by grouping these components. We also prove Makhija's conjecture on products of elementary symmetric polynomials in initial alphabets, allowing repeated alphabets. In this case, the elementary factors are uniquely determined, up to order, by the nonempty Rothe columns.

papers.title: Quantum Evolution Kernel for Node-Attributed Graphs
papers.abstract: We present a novel approach to embed node-attributed graphs onto neutral-atom quantum computers, and propose an application to digit recognition. Our approach extends PASQAL's quantum evolution kernel (QEK) by introducing a node-level feature encoding based on three-level quantum states. To this purpose, we present a prototype showing how the resulting embedding can be leveraged to extract correlation-based information for classification tasks. The entire quantum process is simulated using Pasqal's Pulser library, which inevitably imposes constraints on the size of the experimental datasets. We compare our method with classical baselines to evaluate its potential. We show that, for the digit recognition task, our method achieves a higher mean accuracy than the more commonly used Jensen-Shannon distance-based methods by utilizing the Wasserstein distance.

papers.title: Dependent choice and iterated beta_n-model reflection
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider conservation results for iterated $β_n$-model reflection principles. Using these principles, we characterize the $Π^1_{m+2}$-, $Σ^1_{m+2}$- and $\mathsf{B}(Π^1_{m+2})$-consequences of $Σ^1_{n+1}$-$\mathsf{DC}_0$ and $Σ^1_{n+1}$-$\mathsf{TDC}_0$ for $m \leq n$. Here, $\mathsf{B}(Π^1_{m+2})$ denotes the set of Boolean combinations of $Π^1_{m+2}$-formulas, and $\mathsf{TDC}$ stands for transfinite $\mathsf{DC}$. We also show that, in each case, the stronger theory has a super-exponential speed-up over the corresponding conservative subtheory.

papers.title: Robust global supply chain reconfiguration under tariff and geopolitical uncertainty
papers.abstract: Global supply chains are increasingly exposed to trade policy shocks and physical disruptions arising from common geopolitical events. We develop a robust optimization framework with two decision stages for strategic supply chain reconfiguration. Supplier qualification and transportation arc activation decisions are made before uncertainty is realized, while operational flows adapt afterward.
