We then combine it with a bound on holding and setup costs required by batching to obtain the general-setup guarantee and instance-specific performance bounds for any admissible replenishment policy. In our numerical study, the largest estimated policy-cost-to-lower-bound ratios are about $1.59$ for our heuristic $(r, Q)$ policy and $1.47$ after joint optimization of $r$ and $Q$. The heuristic also performs well against the optimized policy: over the sampled instances, its median extra cost ranges from $2.33\%$ to $3.91\%$, depending on the setup cost.

papers.title: Chain flaring fails on the rose for atoroidal irreducible automorphisms
papers.abstract: We show that the chain flare condition introduced by Clay fails for every topological representative on the topological $n$-rose of every power of an atoroidal irreducible automorphism of $F_n$.

papers.title: Concentration of Exponential Tilts Implies Curvature
papers.abstract: We show, under a smoothness assumption, that probability measures whose exponential tilts have a uniformly bounded variance are given by a strongly convex potential, up to a bounded perturbation, yielding a partial converse to the Bakry-Émery theorem combined with Holley-Stroock's perturbation principle. A stronger version enforcing uniform convexity of the potential is obtained by considering the low-temperature regime.

papers.title: Correlation inequalities for volume polynomials
papers.abstract: We establish sharp correlation inequalities for volume polynomials associated with covers of multisets. These inequalities simultaneously generalize the Khovanskii--Teissier and reverse Khovanskii--Teissier inequalities for intersections of nef divisor classes on projective varieties. They also hold for volume polynomials arising from convex bodies and Hermitian matrices, recovering and extending classical results such as the Alexandrov--Fenchel inequality for mixed volumes of convex bodies and the Hadamard--Fischer inequality for determinants of positive semidefinite matrices. As a combinatorial application, we prove a negative correlation inequality for partitions of bases of matroids that are linearly realizable over a field.

papers.title: Variational principle for the Carathéodory--Pesin entropy of foliations
papers.abstract: We introduce Carathéodory-Pesin structures for non-singular foliations on Riemannian manifolds and define a new notion of entropy for such foliations. Under dynamical and geometric assumptions on the corresponding holonomy pseudogroups, we establish a variational description of this new concept which relates it to the local metric entropy of measures on transversals and to the entropy of harmonic measures on the manifold.

papers.title: Admissible sets of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1
papers.abstract: Let $\mathcal O_K$ be the ring of integers of a number field $K$. A finite subset $\mathcal H=\{η_1,\ldots,η_k\}\subset\mathcal O_K$ is said to be \emph{admissible} if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathcal O_K$, the reductions of the $η_i$ modulo $\mathfrak p$ do not represent every residue class. The diameter of a finite subset $S$ of $\mathcal O_K$ is defined to be \[\mathrm{diam}(S):= \max_{η_i,η_j\in S:η_i\neqη_j}|\mathcal N(η_i-η_j)|\] where $\mathcal N$ denotes the norm down to the rational field. This paper computationally investigates admissible subsets of rings of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1 (such as the Gaussian integers or the Eisenstein integers) that are large relative to their diameter. The motivation is twofold. Firstly, there is the improvement of results analogous to the question of an upper bound for the least gap between large rational primes, which has been one of the great number theoretic successes of the twenty-first century. A second motivation is that there is the opportunity to disprove a variation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. The calculations in the paper provide new records on the smallest distance between primes in the fields in question, and explicit counter-examples to a generalisation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture in all bar one of the fields.

papers.title: Existence of static axisymmetric solutions to the Einstein equations
papers.abstract: We construct smooth Riemannian metrics and scalar potentials that are invariant under a circle action and satisfy the static Einstein equations with positive cosmological constant. The underlying compact three-manifold is a ball with two disjoint open balls removed. The potential (or lapse function) is positive in the interior and vanishes at the boundary, consisting of three non-degenerate horizons. The areas of the two inner boundary components are controlled by two arbitrary parameters, namely the masses of the black holes, which are taken to be sufficiently small and comparable. Each inner horizon radius scales linearly with the individual mass parameters, while the separation of their reference centers scales as the cube root of the total mass. These two scales are assumed to be sufficiently small at different rates, whereas the cosmological length remains fixed. The main analytical challenge is to control the linearized equation and the nonlinear remainder simultaneously near the shrinking horizons, between the centers and in the outer region. Weighted Hölder estimates quantify the growth of the inverse and show that the error of an approximation joining Kottler collars to de Sitter space is small enough to close a contraction argument. Namely, we solve a reduced elliptic Einstein equation that is endowed with two obstruction tensors; varying the two axial positions removes their coefficients. The contracted Bianchi identity and an energy estimate for an auxiliary vector field (Killing field) introduced by the projection to vanish. Finally, for a fixed cosmological constant, the intrinsic metric of one of the two boundary components is sufficient to determine a static solution with simply connected interior and non-vanishing boundary gradient, up to isometry and multiplication of the potential by a positive constant.

papers.title: Inductive Grounded Arithmetic: Goodstein, the Hydra, and $Γ_0$
papers.abstract: What does a recursive definition mean when the logic is grounded, so a sentence is true only if a terminating process makes it so? Kripke's answer for the special case of truth was the least fixed point. This paper takes that answer as a rule. Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) already writes any recursive definition as one self-referential term, paradoxes included. Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA) adds the elimination rule for every positive one, so that accessibility, the winning positions of a game, and grounded truth itself each come with their own induction principle. The rule is sound for the omega model and the system is consistent, both machine-checked in Isabelle/HOL. With the rule, IGA proves Goodstein's theorem outright, in a logic without implication at an undecided hypothesis, and the Kirby-Paris hydra game for primitive recursive strategies, both with every step of the arithmetic a grounded derivation. It proves the Cantor normal forms well-founded, from which the well-foundedness of the standard $\varepsilon_0$ notation system in HOL follows, and it certifies the Veblen notation as an ordinal below every $\varphi(n,0)$. It defines Kripke truth for RGA's own language as one fixed point that agrees with the omega model exactly. Two equivalences locate what the classical world has and the grounded one does not. IGA proves the whole Veblen notation well-founded exactly when it admits bivalence of accessibility for that order, and bivalence of accessibility for an order is sound exactly when the order is well-founded; so $Γ_0$ lies at most one instance of excluded middle away, at the accessibility predicate of the notation, and that instance, the well-foundedness sentence and one membership claim in a primitive-recursive form of Kleene's $\mathcal O$ are interderivable over IGA.

papers.title: Demand Estimation with Unobserved Stockout Substitution: Exact Likelihood Maximization
papers.abstract: When a product is sold out, customers who prefer it may buy a substitute or leave without purchasing. Efficient demand estimation in this setting is challenging when inventory is observed only at replenishments, because the stockout times, and hence the products available to each customer, are unobserved. Estimating demand efficiently under stockout substitution has been a challenging problem since Anupindi et al. (1998), and it has become more pressing as the scale of such problem instances grows thanks to innovations in retailing such as unmanned stores. We provide a complete solution to this problem for the multinomial logit (MNL) model, the most widely used model of customer choice. Using a continuous-time representation of the purchase process developed in Zhou et al. (2026), we show that the exact likelihood and its gradient are one-dimensional integrals, no matter how many products, customers, or stockouts there are. Both can be evaluated at a cost linear in the numbers of products and periods. Our method estimates demand for 2,000 products from 2,000 selling periods in under ten minutes.

papers.title: Experimental Mathematics: Discovering The Half-Derivative from First Principles
papers.abstract: This expository paper grew out of two lectures in Miller's Math 409: The little Questions (Williams College, Fall 2026). We explore fractional derivatives by asking what a ``half-derivative'' might mean if applying it twice is to recover an ordinary derivative. Linearity and a natural guess for the half-derivative of a power function lead to a functional equation related to the classical factorial recurrence. Choosing the familiar Gamma-function extension gives the classical formula \[ \mathscr{D}^{1/2}(x^n) \ =\ \frac{Γ(n+1)}{Γ(n+\tfrac12)}x^{n-1/2}. \] We derive $Γ(n+1)=n!$, evaluate $Γ(1/2)=\sqrtπ$ using the Gaussian integral, and verify the half-derivative formula with an elementary integral. Along the way, we explore how the Gamma function generalizes factorials and binomial coefficients beyond their classical domains, encounter the double factorial, see why the usual product rule fails, and examine the half-derivative of $e^x$. We also explain why the original requirements do not determine a unique operator. The treatment emphasizes motivation, the benefits of experimentation through accessible calculations in test cases, rather than the general theory of fractional calculus.

papers.title: Results for distinct covering systems with a prime minimum modulus $q \ge 11$
papers.abstract: We prove that if the smallest modulus of a covering system is a prime $q \ge 11$, then the sum of the reciprocals of the moduli is at least $1+10^{-28}$. This improves on a previous more general bound of the first two authors in this particular case. We also show that it is impossible to construct a covering system using distinct multiples of $q$ as moduli. Finally, we show as a corollary that it is impossible to construct $10$ distinct covering systems with the property that no modulus is used in more than one of the covering systems.

papers.title: Energy stability of explicit--implicit--null time discretizations for nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with state-dependent coefficients
papers.abstract: We study nonlinear degenerate parabolic equations with state-dependent coefficients admitting a scalar energy potential. The explicit--implicit--null (EIN) method avoids severe time step restrictions of explicit time stepping and costly Newton--Raphson iterations required by a fully implicit treatment of the nonlinearity. Using orthogonal projection of the Kirchhoff transform, we prove nonlinear energy stability for first- to third-order EIN time stepping coupled with a wide range of spatial discretizations that admit self-adjoint positive semidefinite discrete operators. Under an upper bound for the diffusion coefficient on relevant stage segments, two IMEX coefficient conditions yield sufficient stabilization bounds without any time step restriction. The estimates dissipate the original convex energy and allow degenerate diffusion. We also extend the analysis to diffusion systems with a scalar energy potential in a fixed positive definite metric, and to consistent positive-weight quadrature discretizations. Applications include porous-medium flow, nonlinear heat transfer in plasma, and multicomponent diffusion.

papers.title: Convergence of Independence Metropolis-Hastings Algorithms in High Dimensions: Iteration Lengths, Cutoff Profiles, and Diagnostic Unreliability
papers.abstract: We characterize the high-dimensional convergence of the arithmetic mean from the independence Metropolis-Hastings algorithm initialized at its proposal. Convergence is measured in the worst-case expected absolute error over bounded functions. We prove necessary and sufficient conditions for the mean to converge in relation to the importance weight. We precisely describe the logarithmic cutoff profile of the sharp decay to convergence where the relative entropy between the target and proposal determines the required iteration length. These results make connections between the required iterations of independence Metropolis-Hastings and importance sampling. For concentrating Bayesian posteriors, we illustrate how the required iteration time can be estimated providing concrete guidance for simulations. We justify the logarithmic cutoff analysis by showing a standard cutoff phenomenon is absent and prove that popular convergence diagnostics based on simulation output can validate inaccurate simulations.

papers.title: Stationary Measures and Boundary Correlations for Multispecies Half-Line ASEP
papers.abstract: We construct stationary measures of the multispecies ASEP on the positive half-line, with injection of highest-priority particles at the left boundary, using vertex models. Our results extend existing constructions of Martin and Aggarwal-Nicoletti-Petrov for the full-line ASEP to the half-line. For the two-species process, we compute the joint distribution of occupation colors at the first two sites. We also partially address the connection with the half-space ASEP speed process.

papers.title: On the frieze patterns by Conway and Coxeter
papers.abstract: The story of frieze patterns started in 1970s with a paper by Coxeter and two short papers by Conway and Coxeter, one listing questions and the other providing brief answers. During the first three decades it was followed by only a handful of papers observing some further properties of the same objects. Then Propp (2005) and Caldero and Chapoton (2006) established connections between frieze patterns and the recent theory of cluster algebras introduced by Fomin and Zelevinsky in early 2000s. Since then the theory of frieze patterns exploded with new results, and frieze patterns found a wide spectrum of connections in various domains of mathematics, including combinatorics, geometry, representation theory and integrable systems. The literature on frieze patterns grew vastly and continues to expand. In this note we give a brief overview of some of the directions emerging from the papers by Conway and Coxeter and single out core ideas which were later replayed in different contexts.

papers.title: Frangible prime gaps
papers.abstract: A prime gap $(p_n, p_{n+1})$ is \textit{frangible} if the smallest prime divisor of every integer $m$ with $p_n<m<p_{n+1}$ is strictly less than the size of the gap, $p_{n+1}-p_n$. Gafni and Tao recently proved that the number of frangible gaps up to $X$ is $\ll X/\log^2 X$, answering a question of Erdős. They also showed that under the Dickson--Hardy--Littlewood prime tuples conjecture this number is $\sim c X/\log^2 X$ for a constant $c$, for which they obtained a rough estimate. We describe improved methods for estimating this constant under the same hypothesis, and establish that its value lies in $[2.7416, 2.7984]$, confirming a speculation of Gafni and Tao. In addition, we present the results of a complete survey of frangible gaps up to $10^{17}$. An ensuing empirical measurement of $c$ matches our estimate very well.

papers.title: Lax Pair for the Kirchhoff-Pohozaev equation
papers.abstract: We prove that the Kirchhoff-Pohozaev equation on any compact connected Riemannian manifold without boundary admits a Lax pair $(L,B)$, where $L$ is a self-adjoint finite-rank perturbation of the Laplace-Beltrami operator and $B$ is a skew-adjoint operator of finite rank, both depending analytically on the phase space variables. We study the spectrum of $L$ using the perturbative determinant which is known to determine its spectrum and to admit a product representation similar to that of the generating function in KdV. We use this to show that the dynamics of the integrals of motion constructed in \cite{BoitiManfrin2026,BHMP,campos} admits a Lax pair formulation with the same operator $L$ and to get a new proof of the involutivity of these integrals.

papers.title: Generators and Lefschetz properties of general hyperplane arrangement apolar algebras
papers.abstract: Hyperplane arrangements are rich combinatorial, topological, and geometric objects with numerous applications. Apolarity is a method of turning a homogeneous polynomial into a finite graded Gorenstein algebra. Invariants of the apolar algebra of the defining equation of a hyperplane arrangement are invariants of the arrangement itself. We investigate such invariants, including the Hilbert function, minimal generators of the apolar ideal, and Lefschetz properties. The main focus of the article is on combinatorially general arrangements of degree d in dimension n with d between n and 2n-2. In this range, we determine the Hilbert function and conjecture that the same formula is valid for larger values of d too. Minimal generators of the apolar ideal in the initial degree are in natural bijection to the lines of the arrangement. The initial degree characterizes arrangements that are combinatorially general. Finally, we prove that the apolar algebra has the Weak Lefschetz Property and precisely characterize the Weak Lefschetz elements.

papers.title: A graded version of the separator theorem for planar graphs
papers.abstract: We prove that every planar graph on $n$ vertices has a vertex ordering $v_1,v_2,\ldots,v_n$ in which each prefix $\{v_1,\ldots,v_i\}$ is joined to at most $C\sqrt{i}$ elements of $\{v_{i+1},\ldots,v_n\}$, where $C$ is an absolute constant. Consequently, every prefix can be separated from its complement by deleting $O\left(\sqrt{i}\right)$ vertices lying entirely in its complement.

papers.title: Symbolic Direct Construction of Augmented Systems for Levenberg-Marquardt Power Flow
papers.abstract: Levenberg-Marquardt power flow (LMPF) addresses ill-conditioned equations and provides least-squares stationary points for infeasible operating requests. Conventional implementations form damped normal equations, where J^T J introduces fill, squares the spectral condition number of the undamped part, and adds sparse-product cost. We propose an augmented LMPF formulation with a symbolic-permutation-based Jacobian operator that fills the augmented blocks directly. We prove that the matrix is symmetric quasi-definite for positive damping, enabling fixed-order, pivot-free QDLDL factorization. This property also motivates the solver choice: KLU value-only refactorization can reuse an unsuitable pivot order, forcing fresh full factorizations on difficult LMPF trajectories. We further introduce one-probe adaptive trust-region initialization for the radius and damping. Direct assembly is 7.5-11.9x faster than the fastest coordinate-list path and 18.0-58.8x faster than cached normal-equation sparse-product formation; QDLDL reduces numerical refactorization and triangular-solve time by up to 3.40x on identical matrices. Adaptive initialization solves flat-started RTE cases in 19-25 factorizations, 7.5-11.6x faster than reproduced three-step LM. On case2383wp, our 84-iteration run performs 84 factorizations and 168 resolves in 237 ms, versus published times of 200.780-441.72 s with fewer outer iterations, corresponding to speedups of 847-1860x. These results require complete factorization and resolve accounting and reveal initialization and legacy-parameter effects. DC-initialized NR exhibits fast quadratic convergence throughout every tested solvable loading range, motivating clearer, reproducible definitions of ill-conditioned power-flow benchmarks.

papers.title: Mixing zone dynamics for the Saffman-Taylor instability with viscosity jump
papers.abstract: We construct mixing solutions to the incompressible porous media equation for fully unstable Muskat initial data. The mixing zone expands linearly in time around an evolving central interface. Our approach combines the $h$-principle with the inversion of the associated Birkhoff-Rott operator, required when the viscosities differ. A key ingredient is to formulate this inversion in terms of the Saffman-Taylor function rather than the vorticity. This considerably simplifies the analysis and may be of independent interest for the Muskat problem.

papers.title: Regularity of the solution map for the Oldroyd--B model with fractional stress dissipation
papers.abstract: The data-to-solution map of the incompressible Euler equations is continuous but not uniformly continuous on Sobolev spaces, whereas viscosity makes the Navier--Stokes solution map Lipschitz continuous on small data, uniformly in time. This paper identifies the behavior of the solution map for a hybrid system sitting between these two extremes: the incompressible Oldroyd--B model in $\mathbb{R}^d$, $d=2,3$, in the high-Reynolds-number, high-Weissenberg-number regime. The velocity equation is a forced Euler equation and the only dissipation is a fractional diffusion $η(-Δ)^β$, $\frac12\leβ\le1$, acting on stress. We prove that, on the ball of small $H^s$ data ($s>1+\frac d2$) on which global solutions exist, the solution map is Lipschitz continuous with respect to the $H^{r}$-norm, $r=s-(2β-1)$, uniformly for all time, and Lipschitz into the natural dissipation spaces; the constant is explicit and tends to $\sqrt3$ as the size of the data tends to zero. Consequently the map is Hölder continuous into $C_b([0,\infty);H^{s'})$ for every $s'<s$, and is Lipschitz in $H^s$ itself when $β=\frac12$. Thus, although the velocity field is only transported, the solution map behaves like that of the Navier--Stokes equations rather than that of the Euler equations. The proof exploits the damped wave structure generated by the coupling between $u$ and $\nabla\cdotτ$ through a Lyapunov functional with a cross term $(δu,\nabla\cdotδτ)_{H^{r-β}}$, which transfers the stress dissipation to the velocity difference, together with a low-frequency interpolation argument that keeps all Gronwall coefficients integrable on $(0,\infty)$. The loss of $2β-1$ derivatives is exactly the gap between the hidden velocity dissipation of order $2(1-β)$ and the dissipation required by the Lipschitz estimate, and we show that it cannot be reduced by the energy method.

papers.title: Second-Order Steps, Spectral Accuracy: Discrete Parallel Transport of Invariant Subspaces
papers.abstract: Eigensolvers return orthonormal bases of invariant subspaces, but each basis is determined only up to a unitary factor, so bases computed at different parameter values cannot, in general, be interpolated directly. Discrete parallel transport resolves this ambiguity by aligning consecutive bases through the polar factors of their overlaps, but approximates the continuous parallel-transported frame only to second order. We show that the resulting frames can nevertheless be interpolated with spectral accuracy. For analytic families of invariant subspaces sampled at $N+1$ Chebyshev nodes, the computed frames are exact samples of an analytic frame related to the parallel-transported frame by a gauge that remains within $O(N^{-2})$ of the identity throughout a fixed complex neighborhood, uniformly in $N$. Consequently, Chebyshev interpolation approximates this analytic frame with geometric convergence. Moreover, the continuous parallel-transported frame can be recovered to spectral accuracy by solving a small matrix differential equation, without additional eigensolves or derivatives of the underlying matrix family. The results do not require the family to be Hermitian and remain valid through eigenvalue crossings and branch points, provided the selected invariant subspace depends analytically on the parameter. Numerical examples confirm the predicted rates.

papers.title: Certifying Distributionally Robust Decisions from Projection Observations
papers.abstract: A scalar measurement can determine a robust decision without identifying the latent covariance or every decision risk. We study finite Gaussian projection experiments with a fixed mean-plus-standard-deviation target. The observation laws define a set of indistinguishable moment models. We exhibit decisions that agree throughout that set despite unidentified risk values, and give a confidence-set certificate that returns a decision or an unresolved outcome. We prove soundness, necessary abstention for indistinguishable models with incompatible optima, and a fixed-checkpoint certification guarantee. A scalar profile reduces nonlinear risk comparisons to convex inner problems. Across seven synthetic instances, jointly calibrated moment regions give sufficient budgets 21 to 52 times explicit expected-sample information lower bounds. Separately measured stopping times are lower, with zero decision errors in 1,900 simulated streams. These comparisons do not constitute matching bounds, and the guarantees require Gaussian replication.

papers.title: Wave Is All You Need: A Quantum Language Model Based on Fully Connected Quantum Boltzmann Machine
papers.abstract: This work proposes a self-attention mechanism based on the fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine (FC-QBM), and further constructs a fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine language model (FC-QBM-LM) using the mechanism as the core engine. By performing unitary evolution on semantic quantum states, the mechanism implicitly implements positional encoding and self-attention computation, eliminating the need to decompose continuous semantic streams into discrete matrices for explicit matrix multiplication, with the measurement results naturally satisfying the normalization condition. Specifically, this work rigorously derives the computational principle of the self-attention mechanism based on FC-QBM, and demonstrates that this mechanism is mathematically equivalent to the classical self-attention mechanism. The mathematical principles governing the training and generation of FC-QBM-LM are thoroughly derived, and the two corresponding algorithms are subsequently developed. An 8-qubit FC-QBM-LM is finally constructed and trained on the corpus of Tang poetry. Under the 8-qubit setting, the quantum layer implements the entire positional encoding and self-attention computation pipeline with only 44 parameters. In the noiseless scenario, the model exhibits favorable convergence. Furthermore, the quantum circuit proposed in this work, which terminates with Y-axis rotation gates, achieves better convergence than the counterpart terminating with X-axis rotation gates. Under the small-sample regime and across eight distinct noise intensity levels, the model demonstrates strong noise robustness, retaining over 99% of its noiseless convergence performance. Experiments on five-character quatrain generation reveal that the model preliminarily exhibits three core capabilities: associative and divergent thinking, content generation across imagery and human-aligned word ordering.

papers.title: Real-Time Correlation of Relaxation, Dephasing, and Two-level System Dynamics in Transmon Qubits
papers.abstract: Materials improvements in transmon qubits have yielded remarkable advances in qubit lifetimes (T1)and coherence times (T2). However, state-of-the-art superconducting qubits experience temporal fluctuations in their performance, which limit gate fidelities and quantum processor performance. We observe correlated increases in qubit relaxation and dephasing rates that last for minutes to hours, which we call T1 and T2 excursions. Using interleaved lifetime and coherence time measurements, noise spectroscopy, and two-level-system (TLS) spectroscopy, we find that these excursions are caused by single or few strongly-coupled TLS defects that spectrally diffuse into resonance with the qubit frequency. Our measurement protocol provides a powerful tool for understanding the noise sources that cause temporal fluctuations in superconducting qubit performance.

papers.title: Intrinsic Gradient Barriers in Pushforward Deep Generative Models
papers.abstract: Broad classes of deep generative models (DGMs) operate by learning to map a simple source distribution, such as a standard Gaussian, to a complex high-dimensional target distribution. Despite their success, DGMs often empirically struggle to accurately represent distributions with heavy tails or well-separated modes. In this work, we show that these difficulties reflect intrinsic properties of the underlying transport problem rather than particular neural network architectures or training procedures. We establish quantitative lower bounds on the gradients and Jacobians of pushforward mappings that transport log-concave source distributions to such targets. For heavy-tailed target distributions, the required gradient magnitude grows as the target develops increasingly large moments. For multimodal target distributions, the low-probability regions between well-separated modes similarly force large gradients in the transport map. We discuss how such large derivatives relate to trade-offs between expressivity and numerical stability. Our results hold under substantially weaker regularity conditions than previous analyses and remain stable under perturbations of the target distribution. Finally, we show that these obstructions can be mitigated when the goal is approximation of a given density rather than generative modeling. Specifically, we propose simple classes of bijective reparametrizations that can alleviate the difficult geometric structure and reduce the gradient burden placed on the learned generative map. Numerical experiments support our theoretical analysis.

papers.title: Path integral control in the complex plane
papers.abstract: Path integral control is a stochastic optimal control framework that computes optimal policies as weighted averages over state trajectories. It was recently shown that, combined with stochastic quantum trajectories, the path integral control approach constitutes a promising alternative for quantum optimal control. In this work, we propose an extension of path integral control to the complex plane using circular complex Wiener processes. The change of measure is defined on the driving noise space under an exact control-noise matching condition, which also accommodates rank-deficient state diffusions. Applied to stochastic Schrödinger equations, the resulting formalism gives a compact treatment of paired non-Hermitian jump channels with unequal positive dissipation rates and yields cross-entropy-optimal feedback and open-loop control formulas.

papers.title: A symmetric extension of Zhao's series for $ζ(5)$
papers.abstract: We prove a four-parameter extension of Zhao's series for $ζ(5)$. Restricting a Wilf-Zeilberger seed of Au to a hyperplane, we obtain a summand in five parameters with zero sum that is symmetric under all their permutations. Summing it from two different starting points gives two trigonometric closed forms, which we prove by Guillera's periodicity argument. The proof is self-contained, and also gives a companion series for $1/π^2$, which we have not found in the literature. Specializing the parameters at roots of unity, we obtain Borwein-Bradley-type identities whose products depend only on $x^2$, $x^3$, $x^4$ or $x^5$. Their Taylor coefficients are Apéry-like series for odd zeta values and for products of zeta values. In particular, we prove five identities conjectured by Au.

papers.title: Rigorous Lower Bounds for Atomic and Ionic Ground-State Energies
papers.abstract: We establish a new iterative method for computing rigorous lower bounds for the ground-state energies of all atoms and ions. The accuracy of the resulting bounds depends on two ingredients: the quality of the initial energy estimate and the quality of the used upper bound for the maximum number of bound electrons, $N_c(Z)$, as a function of the nuclear charge $Z>0$. In particular, this new method allows us to establish the explicit lower bound $E(N,Z) \geq -0.8710\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for the ground-state energy $E(N,Z)$ of the atom/ion with $N \in \mathbb{N}$ electrons and nuclear charge $Z \in (0,N]$, thereby considerably improving the best known constant $A=(3/2)^{1/3} \approx 1.1447$ in the estimate $E(N,Z) \geq -A\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for $0 < Z \leq N$ and coming much closer to the best possible constant given by the Thomas-Fermi asymptotics $\lim_{N \to \infty} |E(N,N)|N^{-7/3}= -E_{\text{TF}}(1)\approx 0.7687$ derived in Adv. Math., 23(1) by Lieb and Simon. To demonstrate the potential and the limits of our method, we also compute explicit lower bounds for the ground-state energies $E(N,N)$ of all atoms with $2 \leq N \leq 86$ and we compare them with the bounds obtained in J. Chem. Phys., 62(8) by Hertel, Lieb, Thirring and the bounds obtained by Seco in his dissertation. Finally, we also provide a uniqueness result for the expectation values of the kinetic, potential and interaction energies on the ground-state space.

papers.title: Nonparametric Regression on the Circle with Applications to Climate and Environmental Science
papers.abstract: Two important indicators of climate change are the decline in Arctic sea ice area and the increase in average temperatures globally. Both sea ice and temperature exhibit seasonal patterns, making circular regression a natural approach for their analysis. In this paper, we construct computationally tractable Nadaraya-Watson type kernel regression estimators on the unit circle, using rate-optimal kernel density estimators. We introduce a leave-one-out cross-validation procedure for the data-driven selection of the smoothness parameter and evaluate the performance of the proposed estimators through a simulation study covering 48 scenarios, including comparisons with existing local polynomial estimators. We then apply our methodology to historical Arctic sea ice area data and daily temperature observations in Stockholm. The fitted regression functions and their derivatives or finite differences allow us to investigate changes in both the levels and seasonal dynamics of these environmental indicators. In particular, we observe a decline in fitted sea ice area and substantial changes in its seasonal rates of growth and retreat, together with higher fitted temperatures across most of the year in Stockholm during the more recent period in comparison to historical data.

papers.title: Extrapolating learned dynamics across bifurcations based on generalized synchronization
papers.abstract: Predicting dynamics across bifurcations by extrapolating trained models is crucial in diverse fields of physics. Generalized synchronization provides a framework for understanding dynamical reconstruction by neural networks, especially in the context of reservoir computing. Building on this framework, we derive a formula combining pretrained readouts to reconstruct unseen chaotic dynamics. Using classical Lagrange interpolation theory, we derive rigorous bounds on readout errors and conjugacy residuals. Numerical examples demonstrate accurate prediction of chaotic dynamics across bifurcations.

papers.title: Spectra, Growth, and Localization in Half-Bounded Tensor Triangular Geometry
papers.abstract: Over a noetherian scheme, classical cohomological support determines thick tensor ideals of perfect complexes. In half-bounded derived categories, complexes with the same support can generate different radical thick tensor ideals. We study how these distinctions affect the Balmer spectrum and localization. For a commutative noetherian ring $R$, we prove that $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(R))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian. For a nonempty noetherian scheme $X$, the corresponding condition is $\dim X=0$. For such a ring $R$ and a finite group $G$, $\operatorname{Spc}(\mathbf D^-_{\mathrm{fg}}(RG))$ is noetherian if and only if $R$ is artinian and $|G|$ is invertible in $R$. Using the Sanders--Zhang classification over a discrete valuation ring, we compare objects whose annihilator exponents grow at different rates in different degrees. We lift the relevant generation relations before changing coefficients and obtain spectral retractions. These comparisons persist after thick quotients and algebraic localization under explicit uniform annihilation and nonvanishing conditions. A second argument uses nonnilpotent classes of positive degree and passes from cyclic subgroups to finite groups. Applications include relative results for schemes and bounded-below spectra with degreewise finitely generated homotopy. We also describe the cohomological information shared by the resulting ideals. The localization comparisons for bounded-below complexes of finitely generated modules and for bounded-below derived objects with finitely generated cohomology are established separately.

papers.title: New results on nil rings
papers.abstract: For every field~$\Bbbk$, we construct a non-nilpotent nil algebra~$A$ whose Lie algebra $A^{(-)}$ is generated by ten elements. For $\Bbbk = \mathbb Z_p$, its adjoint group can also be generated by ten elements. Moreover, for every field $\Bbbk$ algebraic over its prime subfield, we construct a finitely presented algebra $B$ over $\Bbbk$ whose Jacobson radical is not nil. These results were found with the assistance of Aristotle (Harmonic).

papers.title: Slow blowup solutions for the focusing energy supercritical nonlinear Schrödinger equation
papers.abstract: We consider the focusing energy supercritical nonlinear Schrödinger equation \begin{equation*} i\partial_tψ+Δψ+|ψ|^{2p}ψ=0 \end{equation*} in dimensions $d\geq11$, with $p\in\mathbb N^\ast$, under the Joseph--Lundgren condition $2p+1>p_{JL}(d)$. For every $ν>ν_0(d,p)$, there exists a radial finite-time type II blow-up solution concentrating the ground state $Q$ in the form \begin{equation*} ψ(t,x)=λ^{\frac{1}{p}}(t)Q(λ(t)x)+ζ(t,x),\quad λ(t)=t^{-\frac12-ν}. \end{equation*} All homogeneous Sobolev norms $\|ψ(t)\|_{\dot H^s}$, $1\leq s<s_c$, remain bounded. The radiation converges to a limiting profile \begin{equation*} ζ^*\in \dot H^s(\mathbb R^d), \qquad s_c<s<s_c+2ν|λ_+|, \end{equation*} where $λ_+$ is determined by the leading correction in the asymptotic expansion of $Q$ at infinity. Our proof combines matched asymptotic expansions across three spatial scales with modified energy estimates. The key ingredient is the systematic treatment of the singular nonlinear background and coupled oscillations generated by the slow algebraic tail of $Q$.

papers.title: An Alt-Caffarelli problem for elastic graphs
papers.abstract: We study an Alt-Caffarelli-type free boundary problem for symmetric elastic graphs with fixed boundary height. Our results concern existence of minimizers and their description in terms of regularity and shape. It turns out that the weight coefficient in front of the measure term is decisive for existence. We identify a sharp threshold for this coefficient below which existence is guaranteed. Moreover, we find that all sign-changing minimizers are described by a system of three Eulerian elasticae, none of which are lines. Another result shows non-flatness of free boundary points, a classical question in the study of Alt-Caffarelli problems. These properties lead to a better understanding of the nonexistence phenomenon above the aforementioned weight threshold.

papers.title: Ancilla-free optimal quantum adder
papers.abstract: We construct an exact $n$-bit quantum adder with $O(n)$ gates and $O(\log n)$ depth that requires no ancillary qubits. The circuit uses only $X$, CNOT, and Toffoli gates under all-to-all connectivity and is classically reversible. Our construction accelerates the controlled ladder underlying addition. Grouping the data into blocks and use existing control qubits as conditional workspace gives a recursive construction with $O(n\log\log n)$ gates and $O(\log n)$ depth. We then coordinate inter-block propagation via two short-path forest operations to cut the per-block workspace requirement, yielding a nonrecursive implementation with $O(n)$ gates. Both the gate count and circuit depth are asymptotically optimal.

papers.title: Proof of the Harary--Hill conjecture: an exposition
papers.abstract: The Harary--Hill conjecture states that the crossing number of the complete graph $K_n$ is exactly $\frac{1}{4}\left\lfloor\frac{n}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-1}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-2}{2}\right\rfloor \left\lfloor\frac{n-3}{2}\right\rfloor$. We present a streamlined variant of the proof of this conjecture recently announced by OpenAI (2026). Although the original proof is relatively short, it is quite difficult to follow. We simplify several steps and provide a concise and accessible exposition of the proof. We also combine this new result with known reductions to determine the crossing numbers of several other graph families.

papers.title: On maximum likelihood estimation in the $β$-model for random hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We study maximum likelihood estimation in the $β$-model for random hypergraphs, in which a group of vertices succeeds with a probability that depends on the sum of its members' parameters. The data are independent binary outcomes of experiments on groups of vertices, tested according to an arbitrary, possibly incomplete design. Suppose that every tested group has $k$ vertices and success probability in $[ε,1-ε]$. For complete designs in which every group is tested at least $r$ times, a unique maximum likelihood estimator (MLE) exists with high probability if $r\geq C_kε^{-1}\log n/n^{k-1}$, and for $m$ experiments on uniformly random groups, it suffices that $m\geq C_kε^{-1}n\log n$, where $C_k$ depends only on $k$. Both conditions are linear in $ε^{-1}$ and, for fixed $k$, cannot be improved in general beyond the constant; they follow from finite-sample bounds for arbitrary designs. We bound the mean squared error of the MLE over a parameter box by the smallest eigenvalue of the correlation matrix of the design, and show that the rate is minimax optimal for balanced complete designs. Among $k$-uniform designs with a given number of experiments, designs in which every pair of vertices takes part together in the same number of experiments maximize this eigenvalue, and uniform random designs nearly do so with high probability. Finally, the design matrix of a uniform random design has full column rank with high probability if $m\geq\max\{n,c(n/k)\log n\}$ for fixed $c>2$ and $k=o(n/\log n)$, or $m\geq n$ when $k\geq(1+ξ)\log n$. For fixed $k$, the threshold $(n/k)\log n$ is sharp, and above it rank deficiency is asymptotically as likely as some vertex taking part in no experiment.

papers.title: On Khovanov homology of virtual links
papers.abstract: We show that the Khovanov homology of virtual knots defined by V.O. Manturov and the Khovanov homology defined by D. Tubbenhauer coincide.

papers.title: Envy-Free Allocations for Random Non-Additive Valuations
papers.abstract: Benade et al. (EC 2024) introduced a semi-random model for non-additive fair division in which each agent starts with an arbitrary base valuation over bundles of items and independently permutes the item names uniformly at random. While they proved that envy-free allocations exist with high probability as the number of items grows for $n = 2$ agents, they left open whether the same holds for $n > 2$ agents. We resolve this open question in the affirmative: for any fixed number of agents $n$ and any number of items $m$ divisible by $n$, an envy-free allocation exists with probability $1 - o(1)$ as $m \to \infty$. Our proof combines the second moment method with a connection to the (small-set) expansion of generalized Johnson graphs, which may be of independent interest.

papers.title: Non-Ergodic Markovian Mirror Descent with Unbounded Noise
papers.abstract: We analyze stochastic mirror descent for minimizing a convex objective expressed as an expectation under the stationary distribution of a Markov chain, using noisy subgradient observations along a single sample path. Through Poisson's equation, we decompose the Markovian noise and control its contribution under regularity and moment conditions that allow the stochastic subgradients and the Poisson solution to be unbounded across the state space. We establish an $O(T^{-1/2})$ bound on the expected suboptimality gap of the weighted-average iterate for an appropriately chosen step size. The analysis does not require aperiodicity or convergence of the chain's marginal distributions to stationarity. For irreducible finite-state chains, we verify the required conditions on the Poisson solution and derive explicit bounds that quantify the effect of periodicity. For irreducible countable-state chains, we verify the required regularity and moment conditions under a geometric Lyapunov drift condition and suitable growth bounds on the stochastic subgradients.

papers.title: Emergent Recursive Kernels in Quantum Reservoir Computing
papers.abstract: Learning with a quantum reservoir can be far simpler than simulating its dynamics. We show that a quantum reservoir governed by a fixed evolution, consisting of an input coupling followed by an independently sampled Haar unitary, admits an exact recursive kernel in the large-dimension limit at fixed history length. Memory orthogonality and factorization of propagated overlaps reduce each kernel evaluation to a scalar recurrence, linear in history length and independent of reservoir size. We establish self-averaging around this limit and connect the kernel coefficients to out-of-time-ordered correlators. Our analysis of finite-dimensional effects shows that the computational simplicity of the Haar kernel does not come at the expense of expressive power. Moreover, we demonstrate how the kernel can be tuned for different learning tasks by adjusting properties such as memory retention and temporal interaction order. On the NARMA10 benchmark, the tuned kernel achieves lower prediction error than the tested Ising and Sachdev--Ye--Kitaev reservoirs.

papers.title: Indeterminacy of period map and Griffiths heights for hypersurfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the period map $\overline {\mathcal P}$, from the GIT moduli space of degree $d$ hypersurface $X$ in $\mathbb P^n$ to the Baily-Borel compactification of the period image associated to the middle cohomology $H^{n-1}_{\rm prim}(X,\mathbb Z)$, extends regularly to $X$ if and only if $X$ has at worst nodal singularities (resp. suspensions of slc surface singularities) when $n$ is even (resp. $n$ is odd). This verifies and generalizes Laza-O'Grady's prediction on the indeterminacy locus of the period map for quartic K3s to arbitrary hypersurfaces. For Calabi-Yau hypersurfaces, we prove that the birational map from the GIT moduli space to the BBH compactification extends regularly to $X$ if and only if $X$ has semi-log canonical singularities. The results apply to distinguish the Baily-Borel and BBH compactifications. In the process, we answer two questions of Mordant on the Griffiths height for families of hypersurfaces over curves, which are crucial to the proofs of the main results.

papers.title: A Levi-form criterion for Oka complements
papers.abstract: We prove that if $M$ is a connected Stein manifold of complex dimension at least three with the density property, then $M\setminus K$ is a connected Oka manifold for every nonempty compact $K\Subset M$ with smooth boundary whose Levi form has at least two nonnegative eigenvalues at every boundary point for local defining functions negative on $\operatorname{int}K$. For compact sets in $\mathbb{C}^n$ with smooth boundary, this settles both implications between pseudoconvexity of $\partial K$ and the Oka property of $\mathbb{C}^n\setminus K$: pseudoconvexity is sufficient but not necessary for $n\geq3$, and necessary but not sufficient for $n=2$. In dimension two, we give an explicit compact set in $\mathbb{C}^2$ with strongly pseudoconvex boundary and non-Oka complement.

papers.title: Graham's rearrangement conjecture in finite abelian groups
papers.abstract: Graham conjectured in 1971 that every subset of the nonzero elements of a prime cyclic group admits an ordering with pairwise distinct nonempty partial sums. Recently, the work of Pham and Sauermann, together with earlier results, settled this conjecture for all sufficiently large primes. In this paper, we prove that there is an absolute integer $n_0$ such that every subset $S\subseteq G\setminus\{0\}$ of a finite abelian group with $|S|\ge n_0$ admits such an ordering, which also solves a conjecture of Alspach and Liversidge for all sufficiently large sets. A key ingredient of our proof is a sufficient condition via additive dimension: If $|S|=n$ and $S$ contains a dissociated subset of size at least $Ω((\log n)^2/\log\log n)$, then $S$ has an ordering in which no proper nonempty interval of consecutive terms sums to zero. This bound is within a factor of $O(\log n/\log\log n)$ of the smallest possible additive dimension of an $n$-element set.

papers.title: On the isomorphism of the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$
papers.abstract: Let $1 \leqslant p \leqslant q < \infty$, let $\mathsf{X}$ be a separable $\mathcal{L}_p$-space and let $\mathsf{Y}$ be a separable $\mathcal{L}_q$-space. We show that the space $\mathfrak{L}(\mathsf{X},\mathsf{Y})$ of bounded linear operators from $\mathsf{X}$ into $\mathsf{Y}$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{L}(\ell_p,\ell_q)$ if, and only if, $\mathsf{Y}$ is complemented in its bidual. We also show that $\mathfrak{L}(\mathsf{Z},\ell_{\infty})$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{L}(c_0,\ell_{\infty})$ for every separable $\mathcal{L}_{\infty}$-space $\mathsf{Z}$. This extends and complements the earlier result of Arias and Farmer [On the structure of tensor products of $\ell_p$-spaces, Pacific J. Math.]. Based on this general result, we give a completely different proof of the main result of Astashkin, Leśnik and Maligranda [Isomorphic structure of Cesàro and Tandori spaces, Canad. J. Math.], which states that the space $\mathcal{K}$ and its sequence counterpart $\mathcal{k}$ are isomorphic. Furthermore, we complete the picture by showing that the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$, although isomorphic, are not isometric. Along the way, we show that for every infinite compact metrizable space $K$ the $\ell_{\infty}$-sum of copies of the space $\mathscr{M}(K)$ of regular Borel measures on $K$ is isomorphic to $( \bigoplus_{n=1}^{\infty} L_1[0,1])_{\ell_{\infty}} \approx \mathfrak{L}(\ell_1,L_1[0,1])$. This provides an abstract blueprint for another result of Astashkin, Leśnik and Maligranda, namely that $\mathcal{K}$ is isomorphic to $( \bigoplus_{n=1}^{\infty} \mathscr{M}[0,1])_{\ell_{\infty}}$. Finally, we show that there are models of set theory without the Axiom of Choice in which the spaces $\mathcal{k}$ and $\mathcal{K}$ are no longer isomorphic. This last part was inspired by Väth's paper [The dual space of $L_{\infty}$ is $L_1$, Indag. Math. (N.S.)].

papers.title: Positive solutions of Yamabe-type equations with general potentials
papers.abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$ be a smooth closed connected Riemannian manifold of dimension $n\ge3$, and let $ψ\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. We prove that the equation $$ -\frac{4(n-1)}{n-2}Δ_g u+ψu=u^{\frac{n+2}{n-2}} $$ has a smooth positive solution if and only if its linear part has positive first eigenvalue. In dimensions $n\ge6$, the proof combines an energy estimate under exact local mass constraints with an intersection argument for finite cycles of atomic measures; dimensions $3\le n\le5$ follow from the theorem of Bahri and Brezis.

papers.title: Bosonic Loss Codes with Bounded Occupation
papers.abstract: We study Fock-state codes on $q$ bosonic modes, with total excitation $N$ and at most $B$ excitations per mode, that exactly correct every pattern of at most $δN$ photon losses, for $q$ proportional to $N$. For every fixed cap $B$ and every ratio $q/N>1/B$, we prove explicit achievable rates, positive for all sufficiently small $δ>0$, in logical qubits per excitation. At $B=2$ and $q=N$, the rate is positive for every $δ<0.1355$ and is about $0.281$ at $δ=0.1$, compared with the previously established exact-code qutrit rate of about $0.275$. We also give an explicit upper bound on the dimension of every such exact code, including degenerate codes. For the pure-loss channel truncated to at most $δN$ losses and renormalized, we obtain approximate codes with exponentially small worst-case error. When the loss probability is positive and at most $1/(B+1)$, they improve our positive exact-code rate bounds; at $B=2$, $q=N$, and loss probability $0.1$, they remain positive up to $δ\approx0.158$.

papers.title: Online Discrepancy of Sparse Random Vectors over Long Horizons
papers.abstract: We study online vector balancing for independent sparse random vectors: each arrival is supported on a uniformly random set of $s$ of the $n$ coordinates, with nonzero entries equal to one (binary model) or independent random signs (signed model), and an online algorithm must sign each vector upon arrival. The prefix discrepancy is the largest $\ell_\infty$-norm of the signed sums up to the horizon $T$, the terminal discrepancy that of the sum at time $T$. For binary inputs with $2\le s\le n/2$ and $T=Θ(n)$, Altschuler and Tikhomirov showed that both are of order $\sqrt{s}+\log\log n$; they asked how the prefix discrepancy depends on the horizon and whether a matching terminal bound holds at every prescribed time. Over long horizons, the two differ. For every fixed $s\ge2$ and $c>0$, every online algorithm, even a randomized one that knows the horizon, incurs with high probability prefix discrepancy $Ω(\log\log n+(\log T/\log n)^{α_s})$ for $n\le T\le e^{cn}$, where $α_s=(2^{s-1}-1)/(2^s-1)$. For $s=2$, quadratic Greedy matches this bound; for fixed $s\ge3$, we give an online algorithm with prefix discrepancy $O(\log\log n+(\log T/\log n)^{1/2})$. In contrast, a deterministic algorithm that knows neither the horizon nor the failure probability keeps the terminal discrepancy $O_k(\sqrt{s}+\log\log n)$ at each prescribed time, with failure probability $n^{-k}$ for every fixed $k$, for $2\le s\le n/2$ (binary model) and $2\le s\le n$ (signed model); for $s=2$, quadratic Greedy itself does so. This answers their terminal question, and the same order is optimal for prefixes at all polynomial horizons $T\ge n$. The lower bound uses a finite safety game realized within the input law; the upper bounds use moments of elementary symmetric polynomials and, at terminal times, a $\cosh$ potential or a translated gauge with a Foster inequality at every state.

papers.title: The Plane-Saturation Ratio of Planar Graphs
papers.abstract: For a planar graph \(G\), a plane subgraph \(H\) is plane-saturated with respect to \(G\) if adding any edge to the fixed drawing of \(H\), possibly together with new vertices, either creates a crossing or results in a graph that is not a subgraph of \(G\). The plane-saturation ratio \(\psr(G)\) is the minimum of \(e(H)/e(G)\) over all plane-saturated subgraphs \(H\) of \(G\). For nonnegative integers \(k_1\) and \(k_2\), let \(\cG_{k_1,k_2}\) denote the class of planar graphs in which, for each \(i\in\{1,2\}\), at most \(k_i\) vertices of degree \(i\) have any prescribed neighborhood, where \(k_i=0\) means that vertices of degree \(i\) are forbidden. We prove that every \(G\in\cG_{k_1,k_2}\) with at least one edge satisfies $\psr(G)>\frac{1}{9+k_1+6k_2}.$ This settles two conjectures of Clifton and Salia.

papers.title: The silp--spli equality for group rings
papers.abstract: Let $R$ be an arbitrary associative ring with an identity. In this paper, we show that the equality $\silp(R)=\spli(R)$ implies $\silp(RG)=\spli(RG)$ for any group $G$.

papers.title: On real biquadratic number fields for which the $2$-Iwasawa module has rank $3$
papers.abstract: We investigate the stability of the $2$-rank in the cyclotomic $\mathbb{Z}_2$-extension of real biquadratic number fields. We determine several families of real biquadratic fields $F$ for which the ranks of the $2$-class group $A(F)$ and the associated $2$-Iwasawa module $A_\infty(F)$ are both equal to $3$. More precisely, we provide a complete classification of all fields $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{q},\sqrt{d}),$ where $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ is a prime number and $d$ is an odd positive square-free integer, and all fields $F=\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt{2q},\sqrt{d}),$ where $q\equiv 3\pmod{4}$ is a prime number and $d\equiv 1\pmod{4}$ is a positive square-free integer, for which $ \operatorname{rank}(A(F))=\operatorname{rank}(A_\infty(F))=3.$

papers.title: Lifting $τ$-exceptional sequences
papers.abstract: We study the behaviour of $τ$-exceptional sequences under passage from a finite-dimensional algebra $Λ$ to a factor algebra $Λ/I$. Assuming that $Λ$ is $τ$-tilting finite and that $I\subseteq \operatorname{rad}Λ$, we construct, for every $r$ less than or equal to the number of simple $Λ$-modules, an injective map from the $τ$-exceptional sequences of length $r$ over $Λ/I$ to those over $Λ$. The construction is recursive and is based on lifting indecomposable $τ$-rigid modules and comparing their associated $τ$-perpendicular categories. At each stage, we construct a right exact functor between the relevant $τ$-perpendicular categories which, after identifying them with module categories, is naturally isomorphic to extension of scalars along a quotient $Γ\toΓ/J$, where $J\subseteq \operatorname{rad}Γ$. These functors send each lifted term to an object in the additive closure of the corresponding original term. Finally, we conjecture connections with known bijections for representations of quivers over local algebras and for Nakayama algebras.

papers.title: A note on consequences of Mahler's inequalities
papers.abstract: We derive Makai's inequality $\vol_n(K)\vol_n((K-K)^\circ)\ge(n+1)/n!$ in every dimension from the symmetric Mahler theorem in one higher dimension, with equality precisely for simplices. The proof uses a classical two-layer construction, an identity for its polar volume, and a Rogers--Shephard volume estimate. We then record basic consequences of the Mahler and Makai inequalities for polar successive minima, successive minima at the Santaló point, critical determinants, first covering minima, and non-separable lattice arrangements. We also combine Alexandrov--Fenchel with the volume-product inequalities to obtain sharp bounds for paired mixed volumes.

papers.title: Global Strong Solution to Multi-Dimensional Compressible Quantum Navier-Stokes Equation in Bounded Domains with Large Initial Data
papers.abstract: We consider the compressible quantum Navier-Stokes (QNS) system in a smooth bounded domain, supplemented with a curvature Navier-slip boundary condition for the velocity and a homogeneous Neumann boundary condition for the density. For arbitrarily large initial data away from vacuum, we establish the global existence and uniqueness of strong solutions when the adiabatic index \[ γ\in[1,\infty)\quad\text{for }N=2, \qquad γ\in\left[1,3\right)\quad\text{for }N=3. \] The argument relies on the effective velocity $v=u+\nabla\logρ$, which reveals the parabolic structure of the system. Compared with previous works in the periodic and Cauchy cases, additional difficulties arise from the treatment of boundary terms. We also use a bootstrap argument between the density integrability and the weighted integrability of the effective velocity to enlarge the admissible range of $γ$ from $\left[1,11/4\right)$ to $\left[1,3\right)$. Combining this bootstrap argument with a De Giorgi iteration for the density upper bound and a Nash-Moser type iteration for the positive lower bound, we derive a priori estimates on every finite time interval and extend the local strong solution globally in time. As far as we know, this is the first result on global strong solutions with large initial data for the initial-boundary value problem (IBVP) of the QNS system in bounded domains with compatibility boundary conditions.

papers.title: Recovering the Topology of a Real Plane Algebraic Curve by Tropical Homotopy
papers.abstract: We present a tropical homotopy method for computing the numbers of ovals and unbounded components of a real plane algebraic curve, together with the pairing of its ends at infinity. Under explicit support and nondegeneracy assumptions, the homotopy starts from a tropical patchwork and encounters finitely many events. At Morse event points, the curve changes by local surgery. To determine the global attachments, we follow descending separatrices of a single gradient-like field to a fixed collection of base curves. The order of their landing points defines a finite combinatorial state, updated by local rules that also handle events at infinity and simultaneous event points. This recovers component data without tracing the intervening curves. For the dequantizing lifting, given by the negative logarithms of coefficient magnitudes, we prove an explicit event window when the lifting is generic. For fixed support and coefficient signs, with independent, identically distributed log-normal magnitudes, the expected number of events is bounded by a constant divided by the standard deviation of the logarithms. When all event points are Morse, correctness is conditional on complete, correctly classified event data, a sufficiently small starting parameter, and correctly labelled and ordered landing points. A numerical implementation illustrates its behaviour on sparse curves of high degree and on coefficients spanning many scales; these conditions are not certified.

papers.title: Controlled Block Proximal Linearized Method for Nonconvex and Nonsmooth Optimization
papers.abstract: We consider multiblock nonconvex and nonsmooth optimization without assuming bounded iterates or coercivity of the original objective. We propose the Controlled Block Proximal Linearized (CBPL) method, which incorporates a control potential into block updates while retaining the original objective, variables, and constraints. Under explicit control design conditions and the KL property, the control yields boundedness, finite length, whole-sequence convergence of the original variables, and convergence of objective values. At the limit, one limiting subgradient of the original objective vanishes on all effective comparison directions. We apply CBPL to graph-regularized nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF), CP decomposition, and independent-core matrix tri-factorization (NMTF) with $\ell_0$ norm sparsity constraints. We characterize their reconstruction-preserving scale degeneracies, proving that scale criticality is equivalent to graph collapse and that full criticality forces such collapse. Explicit controls provide compact sublevel sets and a uniform positive lower bound on graph action, including with an independent Tucker core, while retaining genuine reconstruction-changing directions. Each block admits an explicit projection and a computable safe step parameter. For ordinary NMF and CP models, whole-sequence convergence to a full critical point follows. Experiments with direct safe updates demonstrate convergence, sustained graph action, and controlled factor and core scales.

papers.title: The ascending chain condition for radical well-mixed difference ideals
papers.abstract: We establish a finite-basis theorem for radical well-mixed difference ideals in a difference polynomial ring with one endomorphism over an arbitrary difference field. The result extends to every finitely difference-generated difference algebra over such a field and is equivalent to the ascending chain condition for radical well-mixed difference ideals, hence resolving a long-standing open problem in difference algebra. The proof proceeds in two stages. Over an inversive difference coefficient field, we establish a uniform inverse-transform bound relating the perfect closure of a finite system to its radical well-mixed closure. This uses Noetherian induction in a fixed truncated polynomial ring, together with generic freeness and going-down for flat ring homomorphisms. We then prove that the radical well-mixed closure of a system over a difference field $K$ is the contraction of its radical well-mixed closure over the inversive closure of $K$. This contraction result follows from successive prime lifting along flat extensions and removes the inversiveness assumption without requiring the coefficient-field extension to be finitely generated.

papers.title: How characterisations of traces and central elements fail: sharp violation constants via michelson contrast and noncentrality
papers.abstract: A positive functional is a trace if and only if it satisfies any one of many inequalities, the first being Gardner's $|\varphi(X)|\le\varphi(|X|)$; positive central elements are characterised similarly. We ask how strongly these characterisations fail. For $\varphi=\mathrm{Tr}(ρ\,\cdot)$ on a matrix algebra the natural scale is the Michelson contrast $δ$ of the density. For Gardner's inequality the sharp constant depends on $δ$ and on the contrast $δ'$ of $|X|$ only through their product: it is $(1-δ^2δ'^2)^{-1/2}$, the secant of the angle whose sine is $δδ'$. On a finite von Neumann algebra the contrast is the wrong parameter, since every central density gives a trace; the governing parameter is the noncentrality, defined through the central condition number $κ_Z(ρ)$ of the central envelopes of $ρ$ (the largest and smallest elements of Halpern's central spectrum). A transfer principle lifts sharp matrix constants to exact constants in terms of $κ_Z$ in every finite von Neumann algebra. For 38 trace characterisations the constant is exact in 23 cases, has proved bounds in 13 and is known only numerically in two; for instance it is $\cosh(\frac12\lnκ_Z)$ for Gardner's inequality and for the subadditivity of the modulus. On matrix algebras the finite exact violations vanish at the trace to the orders $δ$, $δ^2$ or $δ^4$, and outside factors and abelian algebras no function of the contrast describes the constants. We also find the sharp constants of the Novikov-Tikhonov characterisations of central elements, sharp bounds for three unnormalised trace functionals, and sharp contrast thresholds below which subadditivity of the square root and the power-mean inequality cannot fail. A numerical search, certified as a lower bound for each supremum, supports conjectured values for the remaining inequalities.

papers.title: Holomorphic Tischler fibration theorem for Stein spaces
papers.abstract: We study a holomorphic analogue of Tischler approximation for closed differential forms normalized by a prescribed holomorphic vector field. The main setting consists of connected normal Stein spaces satisfying a degree-one reflexive Poincaré property, with finitely generated first integral homology and a holomorphic $\mathbb C^*$-action admitting a closed normalized reflexive one-form. Under these hypotheses, the given form can be approximated on compact subsets of the regular locus by closed normalized reflexive forms with discrete period groups. When the first Betti number is at least two, the approximating forms may be chosen with rank-two lattice periods. We relate these approximations to holomorphic locally trivial fibrations over quotients of $\mathbb C$, with connected Stein analytic fibers that may be singular. We also establish a finite-equivariant version for suitable Stein quotients and discuss the associated normalization obstructions, including those arising from local singularity topology. Further results concern closed holomorphic time forms, transverse foliations, and the relation between the period groups and the dynamics of complete holomorphic flows. Examples illustrate both the applicability and the limitations of the hypotheses.

papers.title: Contact 3-manifolds with infinitely many rational homology ball Stein fillings
papers.abstract: We construct the first examples of contact $3$-manifolds admitting infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings which are rational homology balls. Our examples are planar. They are obtained by a simple modification of Baykur's recent planar contact $3$-manifold $(Y,ξ)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings, and the fillings are distinguished by their fundamental groups. For one of these rational homology balls we give an explicit Kirby diagram, with a single $1$-handle and a single $2$-handle attached along a trefoil, which exhibits its boundary as $(0,-8)$-surgery on a two-component link. We also identify the smooth topology of Baykur's example: $Y$ is obtained by $(0,-8)$-surgery on the link $7^2_4$, and it is Seifert fibered over the Klein bottle with one exceptional fiber. Finally, we construct further Stein fillings of $(Y,ξ)$, which realize all the groups $\mathbb Z/m\rtimes_{-1}\mathbb Z$, $m\ge0$, as their fundamental groups.

papers.title: Logarithmic asymptotics for polynomial threshold functions
papers.abstract: We count Boolean functions represented as the sign of a real polynomial of bounded degree on the $n$-dimensional cube. We prove that the logarithm of their number is asymptotic to that of the classical hyperplane-arrangement upper bound, uniformly over all degrees, with relative error $O((\log n)^2/n)$. We also obtain sharper additive and relative error estimates in particular degree ranges, including an additive error $O(n^2)$ between the logarithms throughout a small linear degree range and improved bounds just below the central degree. The proof combines probabilistic estimates for Reed--Muller codes with a deletion argument for sets of evaluation vectors, an entropy count, and a sharp-threshold estimate for expected rank deficiency.

papers.title: Counting Admissible Sets of Integers: A Proof of the Erdős--Nicolas--Sárközy Conjecture
papers.abstract: A finite set of positive integers is admissible if any two of its subsets with the same sum have the same cardinality. In 1991, Erdős, Nicolas and Sárközy conjectured that $\log a(N)\asymp\sqrt N$, where $a(N)$ denotes the number of nonempty admissible subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. We prove this conjecture by showing that there are absolute constants $c,C>0$ such that $\exp(c\sqrt N)\le a(N)\le\exp(C\sqrt N)$ for every integer $N\ge4$. The same bounds hold for the number of admissible sets with maximum $N$. For the upper bound, we show that every sufficiently large admissible set $A\subseteq\{1,\ldots,N\}$ contains a subset of proportional size whose doubling constant is $O(N/|A|^2)$.

papers.title: Critical measures and coefficient limits for non-Gaussian holomorphic chaos
papers.abstract: We study critical holomorphic multiplicative chaos with circular iid inputs of unit variance. Writing $R=|X_1|$, we prove that the radially normalized boundary measures converge in probability to a finite measure with almost surely positive mass if and only if $\mathbb{E}[R^2\log(2+R)]<\infty$; otherwise they converge to zero. We obtain distinct sharp criteria for convergence at each fractional order $0<q<1$ for radial approximations and for the full Fourier-radial family. Convergence at every such order is equivalent to an exponential-moment radius of at least two. In the positive-limit class, coefficient vectors normalized by $(\log n)^{1/4}$ and their analytic windows converge stably to Gaussian mixtures determined by the same critical measure. This measure is nonatomic, has full support, and is carried by a set of Hausdorff dimension zero. Coefficient periodograms recover the measure, while scalar and matrix energy normalizations give universal Gaussian limits. Exact weighted tails under $\mathbb{E} I_0(2R)<\infty$, where $I_0$ is the modified Bessel function, and negative mass moments distinguish uncountably many coefficient-limit laws, even modulo deterministic scalar rescaling, within a uniformly bounded input family. This disproves the common-law clause of Gu-Zhang's Question 2 at its fixed normalization. We give conditions for convergence of the original coefficient moments and show that finiteness of the limiting moments alone does not suffice. For inputs with $\log\mathbb{P}(R>u)\sim-λu^α$, $0<α<1$, the coefficient normalization and Gaussian-mixture form persist, but the limit has no finite positive moments; we determine its logarithmic tails. Finally, we prove Hardy nonmembership under finite variance alone and, in the positive-limit class, sharp weighted Bergman criteria for $0<p\le2$ and the boundary Sobolev threshold $s=-1/2$.

papers.title: Sharp diameter estimates via integral geometry
papers.abstract: We prove that the diameter of a closed embedded surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ is always less than the integral of the magnitude of the mean curvature, divided by $π$. We also prove a sharp variant for surfaces with boundary, and apply it to address a conjecture of Miura.

papers.title: Exact Identification of Quantum Correlations in the Minimal Bell Scenario
papers.abstract: Bell nonlocality places the long-standing philosophical disputes over the nature of quantum theory on a mathematically rigorous, experimentally testable footing, positioning quantum mechanics between local realism and the most general no-signaling theories. Yet the precise quantum boundary has remained elusive even in the minimal Bell scenario, where the extreme points generating the set are known. Here we characterize this boundary through a computable necessary and sufficient criterion: a correlation is quantum if and only if it can be decomposed into an extreme quantum correlation and a classical correlation. The criterion follows from our proof that every Bell functional exhibiting quantum advantage admits a unique quantum maximizer. We further classify the finitely many maximal-face structures containing each nonlocal exposed point according to their local deterministic vertices. By sharply distinguishing physically realizable correlations from nonphysical ones, these results resolve a long-standing open problem and provide a new foundation for identifying the principles underlying quantum theory and determining the ultimate information-theoretic limits of quantum correlations.

papers.title: On derived equivalences of exact structures on the category of representations $k[x]/(x^n)$
papers.abstract: From the perspective of homological algebra, exact categories are interesting because they possess derived categories. Typically, an additive category admits many exact structures. If the original category is sufficiently nice (for example, quasi-abelian), a classification of exact structures can be given in terms of certain Serre subcategories in the category of contravariant functors. It turns out that the derived categories of different exact structures are functorially related. This work is concerned with sufficient conditions for the derived equivalence of different exact structures on certain categories.

papers.title: A general algebraic characterization of extremal $Δ$-trees and $k$-cyclic graphs for degree-homogeneous VDB indices
papers.abstract: We present a general algebraic method for maximizing a vertex-degree-based (VDB) topological index $TI(G) = \sum_{uv \in E(G)} f(d(u),d(v))$ over the class of $n$-vertex trees with a prescribed maximum degree $Δ\ge 3$. By expressing the edge multiplicities of the basis $\mathcal{B} = \{(1,Δ), (Δ,Δ)\}$ via degree-sum identities, we reduce the maximization of $TI(T)$ to the minimization of an explicit discrete penalty function $G(x,y)$ over the non-basic edges. We formulate five analytical conditions on the weight function $f(x,y)$ that dictate the optimal edge distributions, yielding a complete characterization of the extremal trees across all congruence classes of $n \pmod{Δ- 1}$. Additionally, we provide their explicit construction by attaching leaves to a core of internal vertices. Applying this framework, we obtain the complete characterization of extremal $Δ$-trees for the Degree-Ratio Sombor ($DRSO$), Symmetric Division Deg ($SDD$), and Hyperbolic Sombor ($HSO$) indices for all $Δ\ge 3$. Furthermore, the analytical conditions identify the exact degree thresholds for the Arithmetic-Geometric ($AG$) and Diminished Sombor ($DSO$) indices, showing that the same extremal family maximizes $AG$ if and only if $3 \le Δ\le 8$, and $DSO$ if and only if $3 \le Δ\le 4$. Finally, since changing the edge count from $m = n - 1$ to $m = n - 1 + k$ affects only the constant term in the decomposition while leaving the penalty function $G(x,y)$ invariant, the method extends directly to connected $k$-cyclic graphs.

papers.title: Global Stability of the Kolmogorov--Zakharov Spectrum for the Wave Kinetic Equation
papers.abstract: We prove global nonlinear stability near the mass Kolmogorov--Zakharov spectrum $f_M(ω)=ω^{-7/6}$ for the isotropic cubic wave kinetic equation, including small time-dependent external forces. For sufficiently small initial perturbations and forcing, the solution remains uniformly close to $f_M$ for all time in a weighted norm. This norm allows $f(t,ω)\sim a_0(t)ω^{-7/6}$ as $ω\to0$ and $f(t,ω)\sim a_\infty(t)ω^{-7/6}$ as $ω\to\infty$. When the external force $φ$ is independent of time, the solution converges at an algebraic rate to a stationary solution in weaker weighted norms. We also give a necessary and sufficient condition on the initial perturbation for convergence in the original weighted norm. These results resolve, for small perturbations of the Kolmogorov--Zakharov spectrum, the question of convergence to a stationary solution under time-independent forcing raised by Collot, Dietert, and Germain (arXiv:2208.00947, Section 1.3). To establish this stability, the collision integral is expanded around $a_0(t)f_M$ at low frequencies and $a_\infty(t)f_M$ at high frequencies, separating it into a linear term with time-dependent coefficients and a nonlinear remainder. This decomposition yields improved control of the nonlinear remainder. The main difficulty is that $a_0(t)$ may vary in time, so the linear operator itself changes with time and its evolution cannot be represented by the semigroup of a single fixed operator. To address this difficulty, we use a parametrix construction to explicitly construct the evolution operator $U_{a_0,a_\infty}$ and establish the required uniform bounds. Moreover, our arguments provide a general framework for proving global stability that may also apply to other evolution equations.

papers.title: Lempert left inverses of the Royal and Flat geodesics of the symmetrized bidisc
papers.abstract: In this note, we give complete description of the Lempert left inverses of the royal and flat geodesics of the symmetrized bidisc.
